## 1. Answers in the requested format

```text
B1: Alternative: accept the proposed six-category contract using the existing
    spellings plus BUDGET:
    MODEL_FAILURE, DATA_FAILURE, BUDGET, INTERNAL_ERROR,
    PERSISTENCE_ERROR, INTERRUPTED.
    BUDGET is an addition requiring implementation and approved tests; the
    other five remain unchanged. It is not currently implemented.

B2: No to renaming MODEL_FAILURE -> MODEL and DATA_FAILURE -> DATA.
    Please use MODEL_FAILURE and DATA_FAILURE in RUN-001. This preserves the
    existing public contract and avoids unnecessary source/test/evidence-reader
    migration. Short human-facing labels may be explained without changing
    serialized values.

B3: Yes in principle, subject to a targeted implementation and tests.
    A distinguishable budget-exhaustion condition and run-scoped exhausted
    state can reach authoritative finalization. Memory/fallback handlers must
    not hide it or turn it into a successful result. Current code does not yet
    guarantee this; see section 3.

B4: Yes: add a budget-exhaustion row to B's runtime-policy catalog and update
    the interface/invariant references together. A should retain the required
    trigger/outcome in RUN-001; B's catalog supplies the operational action.
    One does not replace the other. These updates remain proposed, not done.

B5: A rename would be a breaking serialized-value change for consumers and
    validators expecting the current vocabulary. Retaining the existing names
    avoids needing DATA/MODEL aliases. Preserve old evidence bytes/hashes.
    If a rename is adopted despite this recommendation, explicitly version
    compatibility and legacy reading; never rewrite old records to match.

B6: Pairing is not correct as equivalent coverage. R1/R3/R8 have qualified
    overlap; R2 and R4-R7 have no complete counterpart in the current register.
    Use the corrected crosswalk in section 2. Do not put unrelated rules under
    INV-13 or use a pointer to imply that they are implemented.

B7: Separate machine-readable entries for the adopted distinct invariant
    requirements, with their own statements and zero-tolerance fit criteria.
    The course does not prescribe exactly eight. A lone pointer to a Markdown
    register is insufficient for D1's stated requirement-entry contents.
    Architecture refinements may map one-to-many; retain stable old IDs/status.

B8: Yes to making scoped zero-tolerance criteria explicit in B's register;
    no to treating that Markdown annotation as a replacement for D1 YAML.
    A literal zero_tolerance key is not mandated by the brief: use the agreed
    schema and record metric, threshold=0, scope and verification. A marker
    alone proves neither enforcement nor acceptance.
```

## 2. Corrected invariant crosswalk

These are mappings of meaning, not approval of the new requirements or proof of compliance. Original R1-R8 checker rules, current Q1-Q4 output checks, semantic rubric R1-R7 and runtime-policy R* triggers are different namespaces.

| A's ID / intended rule | Closest current architecture/check | Relationship and required correction |
|---|---|---|
| `REQ-TA-INV-001`: R1 readable final rating | **INV-08**, **INV-03** and **Q1 / SEL-TA-FR-007** | **Partial.** INV-08 controls outcome/rating/check fields; it permits COMPLETED with rating REVIEW. Q1 then requires NEEDS_REVIEW. State the invariant as an unreadable rating never receiving PASSED, not that every completed run must produce a readable investment rating. Preserve COMPLETED/REVIEW versus model failure. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-002`: R2 every cited evidence ID resolves | **No equivalent** | INV-04 binds input provenance to the frozen RunContext; it does not implement a cited-evidence registry. Keep this as an explicitly adopted new/unverified obligation, or disposition it explicitly. Do not claim INV-04 or Q2 satisfies it. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-003`: R3 no banned ownership phrase | **INV-02 + INV-13**, with contextual evaluation | **Partial intent, different mechanism.** Current rules distinguish unknown input, explicit flat input and supplied holdings. They do not ban every occurrence of phrases such as “current position.” Ground assertions in the supplied facts and assess conditional explanations/quotations in context. No current Q rule is a universal ownership classifier. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-004`: R4 sentiment score matches band | **No equivalent** | INV-13 concerns ownership, role labels and Hold/REVIEW semantics, not sentiment score ranges. A needs the actual band definitions and enforcing component/tests if this remains adopted. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-005`: R5 confidence within coverage cap | **No equivalent** | INV-13 defines neither coverage-derived confidence caps nor their correction policy. Do not claim it enforces one. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-006`: R6 no sentiment direction without data | **No equivalent** | INV-13 is not a sentiment-data availability gate. State the exact stage/data scope and fallback if adopted. Missing sentiment data must not silently become a requirement to force the whole application's research rating to Hold when other evidence exists. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-007`: R7 coverage section equals coverage record | **No equivalent** | INV-04 concerns frozen input metadata, and INV-13 concerns portfolio semantics. Neither is a per-channel coverage-record/report equality check. A separate definition/enforcer/negative test is needed if retained. |
| `REQ-TA-INV-008`: R8 disclaimer and guarantee wording | **INV-03**, **Q3/Q4**, **SEL-TA-FR-006/007** | **Partial.** INV-03 assigns deterministic authority; Q3/Q4 specify actual disclaimer/phrase checks. They do not certify absence of every conceivable guarantee. Preserve the defined report-body placement, disclaimer exclusion and phrase inventory; a quoted refusal can still trigger Q4 NEEDS_REVIEW. INV-03 alone is not the complete content rule. |

B's register defines the meanings of its architecture IDs. The team-adopted D1 defines product obligations. An architecture draft should not automatically override a different requirement or erase it through an incorrect pairing. Resolve differences explicitly, then make both artifacts co-evolve.

Retain `REQ-TA-INV-001...008` for stable references. For each, record the truthful status and whether a mapping is equivalent, partial, replaced or deferred. A new source link does not by itself replace the requirement's original meaning. Also cover the other adopted architecture obligations, including consent, privacy, immutable snapshots, shared entry and publication; the eight old checker rules are not the complete architecture invariant set.

## 3. BUDGET boundary and operational policy

The proposed budget condition should be recognized explicitly before generic INTERNAL_ERROR/model-error classification. The run-scoped controller is shared by enabled quick/deep, structured/plain, retry and memory paths. A refusal must stop new reservations; already-issued requests remain accounted for. Broad exception handlers in `agents/structured.py`, `memory/settlement.py` and the graph memory step require special handling or an authoritative exhausted-state check so they cannot hide the stop.

Suggested new policy row, using the next unused ID after the current catalog (currently **R17**):

| Trigger | Responsible component | Action | Normal result | Safe diagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A required model request is refused by an adopted run budget | Run budget controller -> shared execution boundary -> finalizer | Refuse the request, stop new admission, account for in-flight work, preserve available partial content through normal publication | INCOMPLETE / BUDGET; no final rating; NOT_RUN | Budget kind, configured limit, relevant counters and run/attempt identity; no prompts or secrets |

The existing catalog extends beyond R1-R8; do not renumber it or confuse those trigger IDs with the original checker rules. Reaching a numerical cap after the last needed request does not itself require failure: a workflow that finishes within budget may complete. Refusing a required additional request is the stop trigger.

**Preserve existing failure precedence.** If critical report/manifest publication itself fails, INV-14's PERSISTENCE_ERROR remains the primary returned reason; retain the initiating budget cause in safe diagnostics. Do not return misleading published-artifact paths. Ordinary budget exhaustion must not be silently relabelled INTERNAL_ERROR. A/C/B should make simultaneous-cause precedence explicit while retaining one primary stop reason.

Add BUDGET consistently to the result contract, classifier, policy, report/manifest/evidence validators and regression fixtures. Existing validators may reject this new value until updated; an enum addition is not automatically supported by every old reader. Do not weaken strict validation by accepting arbitrary new strings. Proposed tests need human approval before implementation; no passing result is claimed here.

## 4. Two related assumptions to correct

**INTERRUPTED does not settle resume design.** Cooperative interruption fits the existing reason, but “resume keeps run_id and adds an attempt” is a separate contract change. INV-12 currently specifies a fresh run ID per invocation and immutable, non-overwritten published artifacts; INV-11 specifies one logical terminal per run. Reusing the same ID after publishing an interrupted result requires a distinct attempt identity, artifact/event scoping and explicit publication/aggregation rules. Do not approve D-5 implicitly through this vocabulary reply. Keep interruption semantics, and confirm or defer the resume design separately; never overwrite the interrupted attempt's evidence.

**The cited live package has no incomplete attempts.** The 15 deduplicated attempts in `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` are all COMPLETED with `stop_reason=null`. Persistence/interruption behavior is supported by the typed contract and offline fault/interruption tests; it should not be described as an observed incomplete outcome in that live cohort unless another precise artifact is identified. This correction does not invalidate the need to represent those reasons.

## 5. D1 versus D2 and coordination with C

Course requirement-sheet p5 requires a machine-readable entry for every requirement with an ID, type, statement, fit criterion and priority; invariant fits are zero-tolerance. D2 separately asks for the invariant register's sources, enforcement, verification and concrete fallback. Keep both deliverables: A's YAML owns the adopted requirement semantics/fit, while B's register maps them to architecture and operational handling. Avoid conflicting duplicate meanings, not the necessary requirement-to-design trace.

For each adopted invariant, specify a scoped violation metric with threshold 0 and a concrete verification method; a negative fixture must expose a violation. Distinguish deterministic enforcement from contextual semantic assessment. “Zero observed violations in this declared evaluation” does not prove universal model obedience.

On the separate question to C: this reply does not speak for C or certify A's entire registry. `SEL-TA-*` remains resolvable as the working/historical selection used by existing architecture, tests and evidence. A team-adopted final D1 can become the forward baseline with an explicit old-to-new crosswalk; do not globally rename old tests/evidence or assume a provisional YAML has already replaced the working scope. C should identify which accepted criteria each existing test actually verifies.

The relevant result/finalizer/checker, scorer vocabulary, invariant register and runtime catalog show no differences in this comparison. The local working branch was not moved. Choosing the latter requires revising the statement/fit to distinguish authorized continuation from an artifact collision. 100:

102:

## 2. Corrections needed before adopting the five candidate entries

### 2.1 REQ-TA-INV-009: confirmation must allow execution

The first fit currently requires zero dispatches even when an interactive user **confirms**. That would reject correct behavior. Confirm/decline/EOF also cannot be applied identically to a prompt-free API and unattended flags.

Use adapter-specific assertions:

| Entry / condition | Required result |
|---|---|
| Interactive CLI, valid frozen selection, explicit Yes | Transition to `CONFIRMED`, then invoke the shared execution boundary once. |
| Interactive CLI, No or EOF | Cancel before engine execution; zero provider/model requests and zero transmitted holdings payloads. |
| Direct API with an unconfirmed context | Reject before engine construction/execution and provider requests. |
| Direct API with a valid explicitly confirmed context | Invoke one workflow through the shared boundary; do not prompt. |
| Unattended CLI, valid documented explicit mode/as-of flags | Resolve and confirm according to the declared CLI contract, then invoke one workflow without a prompt. Invalid/conflicting/missing required flags reject before execution. |

Count **workflow invocations** separately from provider requests: one TradingAgents workflow normally makes many model calls. This also avoids confusing the invariant with COST-002's call accounting.

Do not require a `run_id` to be created only after consent. `freeze_loaded()` and `freeze_no_portfolio()` already allocate it while constructing a frozen context. Choosing the latter requires revising the statement/fit to distinguish authorized continuation from an artifact collision. I am not approving either implementation or promising its cost; ask D against that precise distinction.

Replace the statement's combined callback/terminal-file wording with:

> Critical report and manifest publication has one commit point. A critical failure before it returns `INCOMPLETE` / `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no final rating and no published paths. Failure to write the staged terminal-event file is best-effort: preserve the intended logical outcome, record `terminal_event.durable=false` in the manifest before commit, and permit publication. After publication, a best-effort callback failure cannot change the logical outcome or mutate the published artifacts or their recorded durability.

A **post-commit callback failure does not make an already-written terminal file non-durable**. Do not change a previously true flag to false or patch an immutable manifest after publication.

The fit also assigns `stop_reason` and rating to the wrong object. Current terminal-event rows contain `event_outcome`, not `stop_reason` or `final_rating`. Assert the event's outcome agrees with the **RunResult**, and assert the result's stop reason, absent rating and absent paths. Do not silently require a new event schema. A successfully persisted incomplete result may have its own report; a **critical publication failure** must not claim published paths.

Cover these branches separately, reusing existing fault tests where they match:

1. Critical report/manifest/rename failure after a private tentative terminal: only the final incomplete logical outcome becomes visible; no earlier completed terminal escapes.
2. Staged terminal append failure: publication succeeds with truthful `durable=false` and the intended outcome preserved.
3. Post-commit callback failure: published outcome and manifest hash remain unchanged; previously recorded file durability remains truthful.
4. Normal completed and engine-incomplete runs: one logical terminal with matching outcome; required fields are present, with nulls allowed where the schema requires them.

Do not promise successful callback delivery when the callback itself is the injected failure, or a durable error record when storage is unavailable. Ten normal samples alone do not test these fault branches.

 ## 4. Advisory versus authoritative data
 
 | Data | Nature | Authority |
 |---|---|---|
 | Model narrative, ratings text, recommendations | **Advisory** | Cannot set `output_check`/`run_outcome`/provenance |
 | Final rating (Buy/Overweight/Hold/Underweight/Sell/REVIEW) | Derived deterministically from the PM output | Reported, but check Q1 only *reads* readability |
 | Frozen snapshot metadata (mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of) | **Authoritative** (trusted state) | Built by input service; used by header/result/check |
 | `output_check` (PASSED/NEEDS_REVIEW/NOT_RUN) + findings | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutputChecker` only |
 | `run_outcome` (COMPLETED/INCOMPLETE) + `stop_reason` | **Authoritative** (deterministic) | `OutcomeFinalizer` only |
 
 The disclaimer and no-portfolio notice are **frozen strings** (selected-requirements §1) and are treated as trusted content, excluded from Q4 phrase scanning.

 ## 5. Workflow (selected C2)
 
 1. **Discover** eligible `.json` files (non-recursive, sorted, symlinks excluded) from `PORTFOLIO_DIR` — or accept explicit `--portfolio PATH` (outside dir allowed; parent not scanned).
 2. **Select** one file, or choose no-portfolio, or cancel.
 3. **Validate/precheck** the frozen bytes; reuse upstream model validation after explicit shape/type/as-of prechecks. Empty positions is valid (flat); no silent fallback.
 4. **Freeze** → `RunContext` (deeply immutable value tuples; full-64 canonical fingerprint; as-of/basis recorded). Consent state `FROZEN`.
 5. **Notice** (portfolio mode; §6) then **confirm** → `CONFIRMED` (default No). Non-interactive: valid flags are the consent expression.
 6. **Run** via the **shared execution service** (`runapi/execution.py`): rejects any `RunContext` not `CONFIRMED`. Holdings reach the provider **only after** confirmation.
 7. **Render body → scrub → single check (Q1–Q4; Q2 inspects the pre-check provenance fragment against explicit trusted metadata) → finalize → build trusted envelope → stage report+manifest (critical) → one atomic directory commit; terminal JSONL append is best-effort.** Incomplete runs bypass the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. The checked body is delivered unchanged; the envelope adds only trusted metadata. Terminal-event durability is decided before the manifest is staged but does not block publication; a terminal-append failure preserves the logical outcome and records `durable=false`. (§ interface-contracts §6–§7).
 8. Pre-run cancellation/rejection starts **no graph, zero LLM calls, no completed run**; a critical persistence failure yields a typed INCOMPLETE result that never contradicts a returned success.
 
 Detailed state machine, schemas, canonicalization, ordering and failure simulations: `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`.
 
 ### 5.1 Synthetic input-mode walkthrough (document example, not a passing test)
 - **Interactive, portfolio:** user sees `a.json`, `b.json`; selects `b.json`; precheck passes; freezes `b` (fingerprint Fb); notice shows basename `b.json`, date D, as-of basis, provider-transmission statement; user answers Yes → `CONFIRMED`; run transmits frozen `b` after consent; report header carries Fb and mode `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`.
 - **Interactive, no portfolio:** empty directory → no-portfolio confirmation with frozen notice; Yes → `CONFIRMED` with `portfolio=None`; header shows `NO_PORTFOLIO`, null file/fingerprint/as-of.
 - **Noninteractive:** `--portfolio b.json --portfolio-as-of D` → freezes b, consent via flags, no prompt. `--without-portfolio` → `NO_PORTFOLIO`. Neither/both → `InputError`, zero calls.
 - **Cancelled:** user answers No at consent → zero graph/LLM, no completed run, counted as a pre-run attempt (NFR-006).

 ## 8A. Engineering contributions (project-specific design)
 
 This section states the team's concrete engineering contributions honestly. The individual mechanisms are **standard software-engineering techniques** (immutability, content hashing, atomic directory replacement, append-before-dispatch ledgers, fail-closed checks). We do **not** claim to have invented them, and a standard technique's use does not by itself establish originality. The contribution is the **problem-specific design, its adaptation across the existing TradingAgents pipeline, and the demonstrated effect** in this application; the professor assesses originality. Each item separates what is **deterministically enforced** from what depends on **model compliance** (pending semantic acceptance).
 
 ### 8A.1 Protected portfolio facts across Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager
 
 - **Concrete problem.** In the baseline the portfolio block reached some decision stages unevenly. A real observed failure (2026-11-18, F9) showed an explicit-empty `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` run completing with deterministic check `PASSED` while the Trader/Portfolio-Manager narrative still spoke of "reducing/retaining existing exposure" — an unsupported account claim. Downstream stages could also inherit an ownership premise asserted upstream (the Research Manager's investment plan) without access to the same supplied facts.
 - **Design decision.** Route the same protected portfolio block through a single helper, `get_portfolio_context_from_state` (`tradingagents/agents/context.py:214`), into **all three** decision stages — Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager — and wrap it in `<protected_context>…</protected_context>` (`protect_context`, `context.py:271`) so context compaction cannot drop it. Absent input yields an explicit "no account ownership is assumed / unknown, not flat" notice; explicit-empty carries a no-nonzero-target instruction; a held book carries the supplied quantity. The stage instruction tells the model to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises (R4). The five research ratings and three Trader actions are unchanged; no rating is forced.
 - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R4 repair (2026-11-21): equalized the block across all three stages and added the corrective instruction. It is a prompt-grounding change, **not** a new authoritative check.
 - **Tradeoff.** Prompt text grows slightly and each stage must be kept consistent; grounding reduces but cannot eliminate unsupported narrative. A deterministic ownership check would be a larger change the current Q1–Q4 checker deliberately does not make.
 - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (R4). **Deterministically enforced:** the trusted facts are delivered to all three stages and survive compaction (prompt-capture tests). **Not enforced deterministically:** that the model's prose never asserts an unsupported position — that is assessed semantically (pending C, GOV-004).
 - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r4_research_manager_context.py` (RM/Trader/PM prompt distinction, shared facts, user-supplied/unverified label surviving compaction, absent≠flat); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`. Source: `tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py:27-52`, `portfolio_manager.py:30-51`, `trader/trader.py:34,82-93`, `context.py:214-273`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`; `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.
 - **Residual limitation.** Prompts cannot guarantee every future narrative; Q1–Q4 does not inspect ownership wording. The concrete demonstration is the **explicit-empty → upstream RM trim error the downstream stages corrected → protected-context repair → fresh RM/Trader/PM prompt evidence** thread recorded in the remediation review (retained diagnostics, not a new experiment run here).
 
 ### 8A.2 Separation of model advice from authoritative provenance/check results (truthful publication and failure handling)
 
 - **Concrete problem.** Model narrative, ratings text and any self-claimed "OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED" are advisory but can be mistaken for authoritative state; and a run can claim success while its artifacts failed to publish, or leave a caller-visible COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run.
 - **Design decision.** Advisory model output is separated from authoritative, deterministic state:
   - **Provenance** is built only from the frozen `RunContext` and a full 64-char SHA-256 over canonical JSON bytes (`runapi/context.py`), never re-read from the file or `final_state`.
   - **Check authority** lives in one non-LLM `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4); model text cannot set or override `output_check` (`runapi/checks.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py::test_tc_fr007_c_model_claim_cannot_override`).
   - **Outcome** is decided by `OutcomeFinalizer` from typed exceptions (`runapi/finalize.py`).
   - **Truthful publication:** report+manifest are **critical** and published by a **single atomic directory rename**; the JSONL terminal event is **best-effort** and its real durability is recorded as `terminal_event.durable` before the immutable manifest is staged (`runapi/persist.py:130-157`). A critical staging/commit failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with no artifact promise. A tentative terminal is staged privately and revealed only after the commit; a post-commit callback failure cannot revise a published COMPLETED result (R5).
 - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R5 repair plus the C2 boundary (`runapi/` modules). These separate advisory from authoritative status and make publication truthfully conditional.
 - **Tradeoff.** More modules and a staging directory; best-effort events mean a run can publish with `durable=false` (stated, not hidden). Not a power-loss durability guarantee.
 - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (Q1–Q4 + R5). **Deterministically enforced:** check authority, provenance identity, conditional result fields, single-commit publication, truthful `durable`. **Residual:** the checker only covers Q1–Q4, not factual accuracy; terminal append remains best-effort.
 - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (rename-failure exposes INCOMPLETE only, manifest-write consistency, terminal-append keeps logical outcome, tentative not exposed pre-commit, single terminal); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr006_provenance.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py`, `test_nfr004_persistence.py`, `test_nfr002_events.py`. Source: `runapi/checks.py`, `runapi/finalize.py`, `runapi/persist.py`, `runapi/events.py`, `runapi/reporting.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.
 - **Residual limitation.** Q1–Q4 certifies only its named rules, not truth or account suitability; publication durability is cooperative, not power-loss-proof. Demonstration: the **publication-failure / counterfeit-terminal negatives** in `test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (offline regression material, not a new live run).

 ### 8A.4 Demonstration types and originality claim
 
 Three distinct deliverables use this material; they are not interchangeable:
 
 - **Video — product demonstration.** Shows before/after behaviour (e.g., optional/empty portfolio, protected facts across stages, advisory-vs-authoritative status, a publication-failure or counterfeit negative) using recorded live **or clearly labelled scripted offline** material. It illustrates the mechanism; it does not itself prove originality or acceptance.
 - **Original-SE explanation.** Explains the project-specific design decisions above: why these facts must be protected across stages, why advisory text is separated from deterministic authority, and why evaluation evidence must bind case/config/artifact. The novelty claim rests on this adaptation and demonstrated effect, **not** on the use of standard techniques.
 - **Traceability/governance evidence.** The retained tests, evidence packages, and (when assembled by E) `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` link requirement → component → test/evidence → monitor. Presence of files or green CI does not by itself prove a gate is enforced or a rubric passed.
 
 **Honesty boundary.** Standard techniques (immutability, hashing, atomic publication, ledgers, fail-closed checks) and compliance with course instructions alone do **not** establish originality. No experiment, approval, or ADD cycle is invented here; the demonstration thread reuses existing tests and retained artifacts. The honest limits (prompt grounding ≠ deterministic ownership enforcement; Q1–Q4 ≠ truth; scorer ≠ human acceptance) are stated above and must stay visible.

+The 24 November requirements snapshot (`requirements.yaml`, `status: proposed_for_adoption`) proposes obligations beyond the implemented `SEL-TA-*` baseline: an R1–R8 deterministic output check with a **corrected** finding class, an evidence-ID registry and per-run coverage record, a run-wide single-use request-budget controller and a `BUDGET` stop reason. The as-built system implements only Q1–Q4, five stop reasons, and input provenance (see interface-contracts §12). This ADR records the **bounded design decisions** needed to make those obligations implementable and testable, without claiming they are adopted or built.
+
+## Decisions (bounded alternatives)
+
+### D1 — Corrected findings may coexist with `PASSED` (approved published target)
+- **Chosen (target):** `Finding.status ∈ {BLOCKING, CORRECTED}`; **any BLOCKING ⇒ `NEEDS_REVIEW`; CORRECTED-only ⇒ `PASSED`**; corrected values recorded (`original`/`corrected`). This is the approved published target.
+- **Alternative (unapproved requirements-change only):** keep blocking-only (as-built). Recorded as a deferral alternative that would require a requirements change; **not** the target. Tradeoff: loses the ability to auto-downgrade (e.g., R5 confidence) while still passing.
+- **Impact:** `Finding`/`CheckResult` types, report rendering, manifest `check_rules_version`, scorer readers — shipped together.
+
+### D2 — R3 ownership check is a deterministic blocking phrase check (target)
+- **Chosen (target):** R3 is a **blocking phrase/pattern check** over the delivered body against A's banned-ownership list; a match ⇒ BLOCKING.
+- **Alternative (requires A/C/team agreement):** contextual handling — flagged only when not grounded in supplied facts, permitting quoted/conditional uses. Not reliably deterministic; would be a semantic-rubric matter. Recorded as an alternative, **not** an advisory replacement.
+- **Impact:** checker rule + fixture list; no model call.
+
+### D3 — Run budget: shared single-use reservation controller
+- **Chosen:** one run-scoped controller; atomic `reserve()` issuing single-use reservations; `dispatch_attempts <= successful_reservations <= CALL_CAP`; SDK `max_retries=0` (reject clients that can't); exhaustion survives broad handlers; persistence failure stays primary.
+- **Alternatives considered:** (a) reusable semaphore — rejects (bounds concurrency, not cumulative calls); (b) counter at high-level invocations with SDK retries on — rejects (cannot guarantee the bound); (c) branch-overshoot allowance — rejects (unnecessary under single-use reservations).
+- **Tradeoff:** strict cap can starve a parallel branch that loses the last slot (stops rather than degrades) — the price of a checkable guarantee.
+
+### D4 — Evidence/coverage as separate registries feeding R2/R7
+- **Chosen:** dedicated `EvidenceRegistry` (stable IDs, resolution) and `CoverageTracker` (12-channel record, `NOT_REQUESTED`), built from tool results, deterministic render; R2/R7 integrate **after** these contracts are agreed.
+- **Alternative:** embed coverage in the checker — rejects (server-side determinism and R7 equality need a record, not a derived glance).
+- **Dependency:** channel↔method map and the two router-bypass call sites to be confirmed by D/C.
+
+### D5 — Resume identity (decision presented separately; not decided here)
+- **Alternatives:** (a) fresh `run_id` per invocation (current INV-12, chosen baseline); (b) logical-run identity + attempt identities with isolated artifacts (D's call; requires revising INV-11/12 wording). **Not chosen here; not promised.** Interruption semantics (`INTERRUPTED`) stay; resume is a separate contract change.
+
+## Consequences
+- Positive: a concrete, testable target for the broader requirements; corrected findings enable auto-downgrade checks without failing; the budget bound is enforceable; evidence/coverage become deterministic.
+- Negative/limits: larger result/report/manifest/scorer surface (version gates required); R3 deterministic phrase check cannot judge context; R5 corrected-only `PASSED` requires every reader to understand `CORRECTED`; evidence registry is the largest implementation risk before the deadline.
+- Preserved: ADR 001 / C2 selection and rationale; Q2 trusted-provenance guard (kept separately from R2); as-built Q1–Q4 behaviour remains the current description until implementation.
+
+## Related
+- Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md)

 # Interface Contracts (Member B)
 
 Status: architecture draft (revised 2026-11-12 per the Stage-3 architecture review; implementation-aligned 2026-11-24). Typed shapes were **proposed design contracts** for C (test seams) and D (implementation). As of `a62b801` they are **implemented** in `tradingagents/runapi/` (verified against source; see §12).  ---
 
 ## 1. Module map and ownership (addresses B3-10)
 
 Paths below **exist in the `a62b801` checkout** (verified 2026-11-24) except where marked *(existing)*. Ownership is by team role.

 **Dependency rule:** `cli/*` → `tradingagents/runapi/*` → (engine, agents, portfolio, reporting). `tradingagents/runapi/*` must **not** import `cli`. This keeps the shared boundary usable without a terminal (B3-01, B3-10).
 
 ---
 
 ## 2. Design types and canonicalization (addresses B3-02, B3-03)
 
 ### 2.1 `InputMode`
 ```
 InputMode = NO_PORTFOLIO | PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED
 ```
 - `NO_PORTFOLIO`: holdings/cash unknown; nothing assumed.
 - `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED`: an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot. An explicitly supplied empty `positions` list is a **flat** snapshot, not missing input.
 
 ### 2.2 Canonical fingerprint bytes (B3-03, F2)
 The new provenance fingerprint is **SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex chars)** over a **canonical JSON byte string** of the normalized snapshot. Exact rules:
 
 1. **Normalized object** contains exactly: `{"cash":…,"currency":…,"positions":[{"ticker":…,"quantity":…,"average_price":…}, …]}`. No other keys participate.
 2. **Key order:** lexicographic ascending at every object level (`sort_keys=True`).
 3. **Encoding:** UTF-8, **no BOM**, **no trailing newline**; bytes are `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")`.
 4. **Separators:** `,` and `:` with **no whitespace** (`separators=(",", ":")`).
 5. **String escaping:** JSON string escaping only (`ensure_ascii=False`, so non-ASCII tickers are emitted as UTF-8, not `\uXXXX`); no additional escaping. Tickers are trimmed and uppercased before serialization.
 6. **Null/default handling:** an absent optional field and an explicit JSON `null` are the **same** and are serialized as the JSON token `null` (`average_price`, `cash`, `currency`).
 7. **Number-token serialization (exact):** every numeric field is first converted by `to_canonical_number(x)`:
    - reject non-finite (`NaN`/`±Inf`) at validation (never reach canonicalization);
    - normalize `-0.0` to `0.0`;
    - if the value is integral and `|x| < 2**53`, emit the **integer token** (e.g., `10`, `1`, `0`), so `1` and `1.0` → token `1`;
    - otherwise emit Python `float.__repr__` (shortest round-trippable decimal, e.g., `150.5`, `0.1`).
    This defines the exact byte token; it is not "whatever JSON does".
 8. **Positions sort — total order (no `None`/float comparison):** sort the canonical **row objects** by the composite key `(ticker_upper, to_canonical_number(quantity), price_key)` where `price_key = (0, 0.0)` when `average_price is None` and `(1, to_canonical_number(average_price))` otherwise (a tagged tuple: null sorts **before** any number; numeric compares numerically). Because `ticker_upper` is a string and is part of the key, **two different broker spellings that normalize to the same symbol but differ in spelling sort by their hashed spelling**, and a full-row tie is impossible unless all three hashed fields are equal (identical rows are interchangeable, so input order cannot change the digest). This is a **total order over every field that participates in the digest**, so reordering input never changes the digest and no valid portfolio is rejected by sorting.
 9. **Symbol spelling:** `ticker` is hashed using the **original spelling** as supplied (trimmed, uppercased). Holdings keep their spelling (`portfolio.py:40-68`); alias matching is a runtime concern, not identity. Two files differing only by broker alias spelling are **different** provenance and therefore **different** digests (both are accepted; ordering above remains total).
 10. **Excluded fields:** `basename`, filesystem path, mtime, `portfolio_as_of`, `as_of_basis`, `mode` are recorded separately in metadata, **not** in the content digest.
 
 > Invariant: INV-05. Upstream truncated 12-char checkpoint fingerprint (`portfolio.py:70-72`, `trading_graph.py:158`) is **preserved unchanged** and unrelated to this digest.
 
 #### 2.2.1 Exact canonical-byte examples (verified against the rules above)
 Row order after sorting is shown; bytes are exactly the string inside quotes.
 
 - **Reason A — null vs numeric price (reversed input):**
   - Input `[("AAPL",10,None),("AAPL",10,2.0)]` and reversed `[("AAPL",10,2.0),("AAPL",10,None)]` both serialize to
     `{"cash":null,"currency":null,"positions":[{"average_price":null,"quantity":10,"ticker":"AAPL"},{"average_price":2,"quantity":10,"ticker":"AAPL"}]}` → **equal digest** (null sorts before numeric; `10`/`2` are integer tokens).
 - **Reason B — broker-alias tie (reversed input):**
   - Input `[("BRK.B",5,100.0),("BRK-B",5,100.0)]` and reversed both serialize to
     `{"cash":null,"currency":null,"positions":[{"average_price":100,"quantity":5,"ticker":"BRK-B"},{"average_price":100,"quantity":5,"ticker":"BRK.B"}]}` → **equal digest** (`"BRK-B"` < `"BRK.B"`; spelling is part of the sort key). Reindexing the **spelling** (e.g., `BRK.B`→`BRK-B` on the other row) is a **different** portfolio by rule 9 and yields a different digest.
 - **Reason C — numeric `1` vs `1.0`:**
   - `[("MSFT",1,50)]` cash `1` and `[("MSFT",1.0,50.0)]` cash `1.0` both serialize to
     `{"cash":1,"currency":null,"positions":[{"average_price":50,"quantity":1,"ticker":"MSFT"}]}` → **equal digest**.
 - **Reason D — missing vs explicit null:** a position with absent `average_price` and one with explicit `null` serialize identically (`"average_price":null`) → **equal digest**.
 - **Reason E — full example with cash:** `[("AAPL",10,150.5),("MSFT",5,None)]`, cash `2500.0`, currency `"USD"` →
   `{"cash":2500,"currency":"USD","positions":[{"average_price":150.5,"quantity":10,"ticker":"AAPL"},{"average_price":null,"quantity":5,"ticker":"MSFT"}]}`
   → SHA-256 `45f07d9eb3359b059525da0cee26f8a9810269dad11ffb4c42e1dcc7072cef72`.
 - **Expected difference:** changing `quantity` from `10` to `10.5`, adding a position, or altering cash/currency changes the digest.
 
 These are **document examples** checked against the written rules, not passing application tests.
 
 ### 2.3 Deep immutability (B3-03)
 Upstream `PortfolioContext` holds a mutable `list[Position]` of mutable model instances. `RunContext` immutability alone is insufficient. Design:
 
 - The frozen snapshot is stored as **immutable value tuples**:
   ```
   FrozenPositions = tuple[tuple[str, float, float | None], ...]   # (ticker, quantity, average_price)
   FrozenSnapshot = (basename, cash: float|None, currency: str|None,
                     positions: FrozenPositions, fingerprint_sha256, portfolio_as_of)
   ```
 - `RunContext` is a frozen dataclass holding these tuples; it exposes **no mutable accessor**.
 - When agents need a `PortfolioContext`, the boundary **constructs a fresh `PortfolioContext`** from the frozen tuples (defensive copy) on each use; it never hands out a shared mutable object. Mutation of that constructed object cannot affect the stored identity.
 - The canonical bytes are computed from the frozen tuples, so they are stable regardless of later copies.
 
 ### 2.4 `RunContext`
 ```
 RunContext (frozen dataclass) {
   run_id: str
   ticker: str
   analysis_date: str
   mode: InputMode
   snapshot: FrozenSnapshot | None      # None ⇔ NO_PORTFOLIO
   unverified_holdings: bool
   provider_transmission_disclosed: bool
   consent_state: FROZEN | CONFIRMED    # see §4
 }
 ```
 `snapshot is None` **iff** `mode == NO_PORTFOLIO`. `consent_state=FROZEN` ⇒ run not authorized; a snapshot existing does **not** authorize (B3-01, §4).
 
 ---
 
 ## 3. Complete schemas and conditional fields (addresses B3-02)
 
 All projections below are **separately defined** and **never** serialize the portfolio payload or full `RunContext`. Field names use the selected spelling.
 
 ### 3.1 `InputError`
 ```
 InputError {
   kind: "MALFORMED_JSON" | "MISSING_POSITIONS" | "MISSING_QUANTITY" | "NONFINITE_NUMBER"
         | "WRONG_SCALAR_TYPE" | "UNREADABLE_PATH" | "AS_OF_MISMATCH" | "FLAG_CONFLICT"
   basename: str | null          # null when path unreadable before basename known
   field: str | null             # e.g. "positions[2].quantity"
   detail: str                   # redacted, no file contents/credentials
 }
 ```
 
 ### 3.2 `Finding`
 ```
 Finding {
   rule: "Q1" | "Q2" | "Q3" | "Q4" | "CHECK_ERROR"
   status: "BLOCKING"
   detail: str                   # redacted
 }
 ```
 
 ### 3.3 `CheckResult` (F3 — case table)
 ```
 CheckResult {
   output_check: "PASSED" | "NEEDS_REVIEW" | "NOT_RUN"
   findings: Finding[]
 }
 ```
 Authoritative case table (**checker is invoked only on the completed path**, §6):
 
 | Case | `output_check` | `findings` | When |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | All rules hold | `PASSED` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Completed run; Q1–Q4 all hold |
 | Any rule broken OR checker exception | `NEEDS_REVIEW` | **≥ 1** blocking finding (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4, or a single `CHECK_ERROR` on exception) | Completed run |
 | Run incomplete | `NOT_RUN` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Checker **not invoked**; assigned by finalizer branch (§6) |
 
 Invariants (H2 — empty-findings equivalence qualified to **completed** runs): **Completed** ⇒ `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` and `NEEDS_REVIEW ⇒ findings≠[]`; **Incomplete** ⇒ `NOT_RUN` with `findings==[]` (checker not invoked). There is no global `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]` — `NOT_RUN` also has empty findings.
 
 ### 3.4 `RunResult` (returned to caller)
 ```
 RunResult {
   run_id: str
   ticker: str
   analysis_date: str
   input_mode: InputMode
   run_outcome: "COMPLETED" | "INCOMPLETE"
   stop_reason: null | "MODEL_FAILURE" | "DATA_FAILURE" | "INTERNAL_ERROR"
                | "PERSISTENCE_ERROR" | "INTERRUPTED"
   final_rating: null | "Buy" | "Overweight" | "Hold" | "Underweight" | "Sell" | "REVIEW"
   output_check: "PASSED" | "NEEDS_REVIEW" | "NOT_RUN"
   findings: Finding[]
   manifest_path: str | null     # non-null iff the run directory was published (§7)
   report_path: str | null       # non-null iff the report was published (§7)
 }
 ```
 **Conditional fields (enforced by finalizer):**
 - `COMPLETED` ⇒ `final_rating != null` and `stop_reason == null`.
 - `INCOMPLETE` ⇒ `final_rating == null`, `output_check == "NOT_RUN"`, `findings == []`, `stop_reason != null`.
 
 ### 3.5 Safe input metadata projection (for sinks; never the payload)
 ```
 SafeInputMetadata {
   run_id, ticker, analysis_date,
   input_mode: InputMode,
   basename: str | null,                 # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO
   fingerprint_sha256: str | null,       # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO (64 hex)
   portfolio_as_of: str | null,          # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO
   as_of_basis: "USER_CONFIRMED" | null  # null iff NO_PORTFOLIO
 }
 ```
 The `null` conditions are **portfolio-only** (mode-dependent); distinct from **outcome-conditional** `RunResult` fields.
 
 ### 3.6 `SafeRunMetadata` (durable run record; never the payload) — F3
 ```
 SafeRunMetadata {
   schema_version: "1",
   run_id, ticker, analysis_date, input_mode,
   basename: str|null, fingerprint_sha256: str|null, portfolio_as_of: str|null, as_of_basis: "USER_CONFIRMED"|null,
   run_outcome: "COMPLETED" | "INCOMPLETE",
   stop_reason: ... | null,               # §3.4 conditional
   final_rating: ... | null,              # §3.4 conditional — NOW CARRIED IN THE DURABLE RECORD
   output_check: "PASSED" | "NEEDS_REVIEW" | "NOT_RUN",
   findings: Finding[],
   code_version: str,                     # tradingagents.__version__
   source_revision: str | null,           # separate source identifier, e.g. git describe or "unknown" (§3.7)
   prompt_hash: str,                      # §3.8
   effective_config: EffectiveConfig,     # §3.7
   start_ts_utc: str, end_ts_utc: str     # ISO-8601 UTC; set once at finalize
 }
 ```
 The **same** `final_rating` spelling/conditional rules as `RunResult` apply. Timestamps are captured once at finalize and are never mutated later.
 
 ### 3.7 `EffectiveConfig` (safe, behaviour-relevant; secrets/endpoints omitted) — F3
 ```
 EffectiveConfig {
   llm_provider, deep_think_provider, deep_think_llm, quick_think_provider, quick_think_llm,
   analysts: str[], max_debate_rounds: int, max_risk_discuss_rounds: int,
   output_language: str,
   temperature: float | null, max_tokens: int | null,          # behaviour-affecting (baseline keys if set)
   context_cap_tokens: int, compaction_threshold_tokens: int,  # the designed context budget (ADR §Context)
   data_vendors: map, tool_vendors: map
 }
 ```
 Derived from `run_settings()` (`trading_graph.py:255-275`) **plus** the behaviour-affecting keys this design introduces (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, context cap/threshold). `backend_url`, keys, OAuth tokens, local paths are **never** included. `source_revision` is recorded **separately** from `code_version` (upstream `version` stays `0.7.1`; the revision id identifies the actual source state and is `"unknown"` when unavailable).
 
 ### 3.8 `prompt_hash` (deterministic input spec) — F3
 - Inventory: the **template set** actually used = (a) identity/context instruction templates, (b) selected analyst templates, (c) trader + research/portfolio-manager templates, (d) frozen notice/disclaimer strings, (e) the mode-aware legend variants selected for this run.
 - Serialization: an ordered list `[(template_id, template_text), …]` sorted by `template_id`; each entry serialized as `template_id + "\n" + template_text`; entries joined by `"\n\n"`; UTF-8, no BOM, no trailing newline; `prompt_hash = SHA-256(bytes)` (64 hex).
 - **Dynamic holdings/evidence are excluded** (they vary per run and are captured by the fingerprint/state, not the prompt template). Editing any template or frozen string changes `prompt_hash`. `template_id` values are stable identifiers (e.g., `analyst.market`, `trader`, `manager.portfolio`, `frozen.disclaimer`, `legend.no_portfolio`).
 
 ### 3.9 `Event` (JSONL)
 ```
 Event {
   run_id, ticker,
   node: "input" | "engine" | "output",
   ts: str (UTC ISO-8601),
   elapsed_ms: int (>=0, monotonic),
   event: str,                 # e.g. input.selection, input.consent, run.terminal, output.check, output.persist
   event_outcome: str          # progress vocabulary, separate from run_outcome
 }
 ```
 Exactly one `event=run.terminal` logical decision per run (§7.5).
 
 ### 3.10 Final manifest (`manifest.json`) — F1/F3
 ```
 Manifest = SafeRunMetadata + {
   report_paths: { markdown: str|null, html: str|null },
   terminal_event: { logical: "run.terminal", durable: bool }   # durable = JSONL terminal write succeeded before publication
 }
 ```
 The manifest is written **once**, atomically, **as part of the single publication commit** (§7), and contains **no** positions/cash/other-position list and no secrets. `terminal_event.durable` is known **before** publication because the terminal event is written **before** the commit (or its outcome is decided then) — a later append never changes the immutable manifest.

 ## 4. Input-mode state machine (addresses B3-08; both modes complete)
 
 Interactive discovery/consent lives only in `cli/input_ui.py`. The **noninteractive service** (`input_service.py`) accepts explicit inputs/paths.
 
 ```
 START
  ├─ explicit --portfolio PATH ─────────────► VALIDATING_EXPLICIT
  ├─ explicit --without-portfolio ──────────► NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE
  └─ interactive, no explicit flags ────────► DISCOVERING
 DISCOVERING
  ├─ eligible files present ──► SELECTING ──cancel──► CANCELLED
  ├─ missing or empty dir ────► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM   (never described as "empty" if errored)
  └─ directory read error ────► DIR_ERROR ──retry──► DISCOVERING
                               └──choose no-portfolio──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM
                               └──cancel──► CANCELLED
 SELECTING ──file chosen──► VALIDATING
 VALIDATING ──invalid──► INVALID ──reselect──► SELECTING / ──cancel──► CANCELLED
 VALIDATING_EXPLICIT ──(noninteractive: --portfolio-as-of D required, D == analysis date)──►
    ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE   ──invalid/as-of-mismatch/flags-conflict──► INPUT_ERROR (zero run)
 VALIDATING ──valid──► PORTFOLIO_FREEZE
 PORTFOLIO_FREEZE  (freeze bytes → FrozenSnapshot; consent_state=FROZEN)
    ──interactive: show notice (basename, D, unverified/as-of, provider-transmission)──► AWAITING_CONSENT
    ──noninteractive: explicit --portfolio already expresses consent──► CONFIRMED
 AWAITING_CONSENT ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED
 NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE
    ──interactive: show frozen no-portfolio notice──► NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM
    ──noninteractive: --without-portfolio expresses consent──► CONFIRMED
 NO_PORTFOLIO_CONFIRM ──yes──► CONFIRMED ; ──no/EOF──► CANCELLED
 CONFIRMED ──► RUNNING
 CANCELLED / INPUT_ERROR → zero graph, zero LLM, no completed run
 ```
 
 - **Both modes** reach a frozen candidate and explicit confirmation (interactive) or explicit flag consent (noninteractive).
 - **Noninteractive flag rules:** neither `--portfolio` nor `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR` (zero calls); **both** ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio` without `--portfolio-as-of` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of` with `--without-portfolio` ⇒ `INPUT_ERROR`; `--portfolio-as-of D` ≠ analysis date ⇒ `AS_OF_MISMATCH`.
 
 ### 4.1 Consent as explicit transitions (B3-01; immutability ≠ bypass prevention)
 | From | Trigger | To | Guard |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | `FROZEN` (PORTFOLIO_FREEZE/NO_PORTFOLIO_FREEZE) | interactive Yes, or valid explicit flag | `CONFIRMED` | notice for portfolio shown first (interactive) |
 | `FROZEN` | interactive No/EOF/cancel | `CANCELLED` | zero run |
 | `CONFIRMED` | (any) | `RUNNING` | **only** path to `execution.run` |
 
 `execution.run_analysis_api` **rejects** a `RunContext` whose `consent_state != CONFIRMED`. A frozen snapshot existing does **not** authorize execution; the transition does.
 
 - **No silent reread:** after freeze the file is never reopened; frozen bytes are the sole input.
 - **Disclosure sequencing:** only the **notice** precedes consent; holdings are transmitted to the provider **only after** `CONFIRMED` (during `RUNNING`). No provider transmission before consent.

 ## 5. Shared CLI/API execution boundary (addresses B3-01, B3-10)
 
 The **common application entry service** routes **every supported entry point** through the mandatory checks/finalization/persistence:
 
 ```
 # tradingagents/runapi/execution.py  (prompt-free; no cli import)
 run_analysis_api(
     run_context: RunContext,          # consent_state must be CONFIRMED
     graph_factory: Callable[..., Engine],  # injectable for tests; default TradingAgentsGraph
     event_sink: EventSink,
     redactor: Redactor,
 ) -> RunResult
 sequence: validate_consent → engine.stream_run(portfolio or None)
           → render_body → check → finalize → stage → publish → terminal event
 ```
 
 ### 5.1 Entry points and which boundary they traverse
 | Entry point | Interaction | Boundary traversal | Requirement coverage |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | CLI interactive (`cli/main.py`) | prompts in `cli/input_ui.py` | freezes+confirm → `run_analysis_api` | Full (FR/NFR) |
 | CLI noninteractive (flags) | none | flags → freeze → `run_analysis_api` | Full |
 | **Supported project API** (`tradingagents.runapi.execution.run_analysis_api`) | none | supplies a `RunContext` (built via input service or explicit `portfolio`/`None`) → `run_analysis_api` | Full |
 | Low-level engine primitive (`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run`) | none | **raw**; **does not** traverse the boundary | **Reduced** — see §5.3 |
 
 ### 5.2 Supported project API signature
 The upstream engine signature is **preserved** (`trading_graph.py:167,293`: `portfolio=None|PortfolioContext`). A programmatic caller wanting the full contract uses:
 ```
 from tradingagents.runapi.execution import run_analysis_api
 from tradingagents.runapi.input_service import freeze_explicit  # builds a FROZEN RunContext
 ctx_frozen = freeze_explicit(ticker, analysis_date, portfolio=PortfolioContext(...) | None)  # no prompt; consent_state=FROZEN
 ctx_confirmed = ctx_frozen.confirm()                      # explicit programmatic consent transition
 result: RunResult = run_analysis_api(ctx_confirmed, event_sink=..., redactor=...)
 ```
 - **Consent is consistent across all entry points:** `freeze_explicit` **always** returns `consent_state=FROZEN`; a programmatic caller must perform an explicit `confirm()` transition (the programmatic expression of consent; no prompt, no provider transmission before `run_analysis_api`). This matches the CLI/interactive rule that a frozen context is not executable.
 - `freeze_explicit(..., portfolio=None)` ⇒ `NO_PORTFOLIO` RunContext with `basename/fingerprint/as_of=null`. `portfolio=PortfolioContext(...)` (in-memory) ⇒ frozen snapshot with **synthetic provenance**: `basename="<in-memory>"`, `fingerprint_sha256=<64-hex over §2.2 canonical bytes>`, `portfolio_as_of=<analysis_date>`, `as_of_basis="USER_CONFIRMED"` (the caller asserts the in-memory book is intended for that date).
 - This path runs checks/finalization/redaction/single-commit publication — no compliance gap (B3-01 resolved at design level).
 
 ### 5.3 Low-level primitive (precise scope; A approval required for reduced coverage)
 `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate/stream_run/create_run_state` remain available unchanged for baseline compatibility and upstream tests. They **do not** provide the output checker, outcome finalizer, redaction, manifest or events. Scope and honesty:
 - Use is legitimate for baseline/existing upstream behaviour and for engine-level tests only.
 - A caller using **only** the raw primitive **does not** satisfy FR-006/FR-007/NFR-002/003/004. This is a **declared, scoped low-level compatibility path**; **A must approve** any excluded requirement coverage if a product-facing path relies on it (R-API, pending A). It is not a D design task; only A's acceptance of reduced coverage is pending.
 - **Mandatory CLI traversal:** the CLI (`cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py`) **must** call `run_analysis_api` for all product runs; it may not call the raw primitive directly. The raw primitive is not a product entry point.

 ## 6. Render / check / final envelope ordering (addresses B3-04)
 
 **Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.
 
 ### 6.1 Two-part document
 - **Body** (model-generated sections + trusted frozen notice/disclaimer): rendered once from `final_state` + `RunContext`, **redacted before check**.
 - **Pre-check provenance fragment** (trusted, deterministic): the exact header lines Q2 will inspect — analysis date, input mode, basename, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis — rendered from `SafeInputMetadata` **before** the check. This is the object Q2 compares; it is not the checker comparing metadata to itself, because it is an independently produced text fragment.
 - **Envelope** (trusted): the final delivered header, built **after** the check from `SafeRunMetadata` (which now includes outcome/check). It must byte-match the pre-check provenance fragment for its Q2 fields (verified again before publication, §6.4).
 
 ### 6.2 Single authoritative check — completed path only (F4)
 ```
 1. final_state  (or an exception → go to 6.3 INCOMPLETE branch; checker NOT called)
 2. body = render_body(final_state, RunContext)                 # trusted strings inserted
 3. body = redactor.scrub(body)                                 # redaction BEFORE check
 4. provenance_fragment = render_provenance(SafeInputMetadata)  # trusted header text Q2 inspects
 5. final_rating = run_rating(final_state)  |  REVIEW           # deterministic
 6. CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(                        # ONE authoritative call
         trusted: SafeInputMetadata,     # Q2 authoritative expected values (explicit argument)
         provenance_fragment: str,       # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text, compared to `trusted`)
         final_rating: str,              # Q1 subject
         rendered_body: str)             # Q3/Q4 subject (disclaimer excluded from Q4)
    # if the checker raises → CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]} (fail closed, single decision)
 7. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=True, final_rating, exc=None)  # COMPLETED
 8. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # uses the FROZEN CheckResult; no second verdict
 9. verify_envelope_header_matches(envelope, trusted)     # publication-time guard vs AUTHORITATIVE metadata (§6.4)
 10. final_doc_md = envelope + body ; final_doc_html = render_html(envelope, body)
 11. stage → single publication commit (§7)
 ```
 - The checker is invoked **exactly once** on the completed path; the envelope consumes the **frozen** `CheckResult`.
 - **Q2 has a real subject and explicit trusted values:** Q2 compares `provenance_fragment` (independently rendered pre-check text) against the **explicitly supplied trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument. A fragment whose basename/fingerprint/as-of differs from trusted metadata produces a **Q2** finding, not a guaranteed pass. The trusted metadata is a call argument, not ambient state.
 
 ### 6.3 Incomplete branch — checker bypassed (F4)
 ```
 1. engine raised OR graph did not return a usable final_state
 2. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=False, final_rating=None, exc=exc)
 3. CheckResult = CheckResult{output_check:"NOT_RUN", findings:[]}   # assigned directly; checker NOT invoked
 4. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # INCOMPLETE, NOT_RUN, no rating
 5. no successful report body is published as PASSED; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7)
 ```
 The checker signature never receives graph-returned data on this path, so there is no contradictory double verdict.
 
 ### 6.4 Envelope verification and source-of-truth (F4, H3)
 - `OutputChecker.evaluate(trusted, provenance_fragment, final_rating, rendered_body)` calls no provider. Q1 = rating readable; **Q2 = every Q2 field in `provenance_fragment` equals the explicit trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** argument; Q3 = disclaimer present in body; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent in body (disclaimer excluded).
 - **Publication-time guard — against authoritative metadata:** before the commit, the build verifies that the envelope's Q2 fields equal the **trusted `SafeInputMetadata`** (the same authoritative expected values). The guard does **not** compare the envelope to the possibly-defective `provenance_fragment`; it validates both the fragment's finding (already recorded by the checker) and the delivered envelope against the authoritative values.
 - **Q2-defect path (consistent):** if the fragment disagrees with trusted metadata, the checker records a `Q2` finding (`NEEDS_REVIEW`) and that finding is **retained**; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (a **corrected** header) and passes the guard because it matches authoritative values. The run delivers the corrected header labelled `NEEDS_REVIEW` with the original Q2 finding — it is neither silently marked clean nor claimed to have equal-but-unequal values.
 - **Single source for the disclaimer:** the disclaimer is rendered **once** into the body from the frozen string; the envelope references its presence (Q3) rather than re-emitting a second copy, avoiding body/envelope duplication mismatch.
 - **Redaction precedes checks**, so a checked artifact cannot later be invalidated by redaction.
 
 ### 6.5 Walkthroughs (synthetic; document examples; verified against §6.2–§6.4)
 - **Completed-PASS (no-portfolio):** `final_rating="Hold"`; `provenance_fragment` renders `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, basename/fingerprint/as-of `null`; body has disclaimer, no prohibited phrase → `CheckResult{PASSED,[]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, stop_reason=null, final_rating="Hold", output_check=PASSED}`; envelope shows PASSED; guard passes (envelope matches trusted metadata).
 - **Completed-REVIEW (Q2 defect):** renderer bug renders `basename="c.json"` in the `provenance_fragment` while trusted `SafeInputMetadata.basename="b.json"` → Q2 fails on the single checker call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q2]}` (finding retained); `RunResult{COMPLETED, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`; the envelope is built from trusted metadata (`b.json`, corrected) and the guard passes because it matches the **authoritative** metadata; the delivered header shows `b.json` and the retained Q2 finding, outcome not silently clean.
 - **Completed-REVIEW (Q4):** body contains `guaranteed profit` outside disclaimer → `Finding{Q4}`; `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
 - **Checker-error:** checker raises on the single call → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]}`; graph returned so `COMPLETED`; `output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW`; no second call to disagree.
 - **Graph-failure (INCOMPLETE):** exception → INCOMPLETE branch; **checker not invoked**; `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `final_rating=null`, `stop_reason` set; nothing published as PASSED.
 
 ### 6.6 Rendering order for agents (identity vs display)
 Canonicalization sorts positions for hashing; `PortfolioContext.render()` keeps upstream ordering for the prompt. Identity and display are intentionally separate; neither mutates the frozen tuple.

 ## 7. Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)
 
 ### 7.1 Single publication commit point
 The run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:
 ```
 STAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run
   reports/complete_report.md  (and .html if enabled)   # final envelope + checked body
   manifest.json                                        # fully populated incl. terminal_event.durable
 COMMIT:  os.replace/rename  <results>/_staging/<run_id>  ->  <results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/
 ```
 - **One commit point.** Everything the manifest describes (report MD/HTML, manifest itself) is written into the **staging** directory **first**; the **only** publication action is a single atomic directory rename. Before the rename, nothing exists at the published path; after it, a complete, self-consistent run directory exists.
 - **No success is visible before the commit.** There is no earlier `rename` of the report into the published location; the "report staged but unpublished" state is real because the report lives only under `_staging`.
 - **Terminal event ordering (truthful durability):** the **logical** terminal decision is computed before commit. The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.
 - **Caller-visible terminal is resolved on commit (R5).** The terminal is first **staged privately** on the `EventSink` (included in the staged `events.jsonl` for durability, but not in the caller-inspectable `events`). Only after the single directory rename succeeds is the tentative terminal **committed** into the caller-visible event list (`commit_terminal`). If the critical report/manifest staging or the rename fails, the tentative terminal is **discarded** and `run_analysis_api` emits exactly one matching `INCOMPLETE` terminal, so a caller-owned sink can never retain a COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run. The post-rename reveal is a **best-effort callback**: its failure does not revise the already-published logical outcome. Normal completed and engine-incomplete runs still expose exactly one matching terminal. The single-terminal rule is preserved. A legacy sink without the staging protocol has the terminal written into the staged file (truthful `durable`) and the one terminal emitted after the rename.
 - **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. Readers may ignore `_staging`.
 
 ### 7.2 Sink criticality
 | Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |
 |---|---|---|
 | Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |
 | Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |
 | JSONL terminal event | **Best-effort (not critical)** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` but **does not** block publication and does **not** change the logical outcome |
 | Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |
 | State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |
 
 ### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)
 - **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).
 - **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
 - **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.
 - **Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** the **logical outcome is preserved** (`COMPLETED` if the graph returned); `terminal_event.durable=false` is recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; the run directory is still published (report+manifest valid). This is **not** a critical failure and does **not** return `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
 - **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical report/manifest staging-or-commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result. On such a failure the stage-private tentative terminal is discarded and exactly one `INCOMPLETE` terminal is emitted to the caller sink (R5).
 - **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.
 
 ### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization
 `OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.
 
 ### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)
 Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.
 
 - **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.
 - **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.
 - **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.
 - **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.
 - **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the **logical outcome** (COMPLETED if graph returned) — **not** PERSISTENCE_ERROR; a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.
 
 No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.

   output_check: "PASSED" | "NEEDS_REVIEW" | "NOT_RUN" | null
   stop_reason: ... | null
   controlled_change: {factor: str, value: str} | null   # for before/after experiments
 ```
 Aggregation (design):
 - `completion_fraction = count(category=STARTED and run_outcome=COMPLETED) / count(category=STARTED)` (pre-run categories excluded from the denominator but reported separately).
 - Report `completed_count`, `needs_review_count`, `incomplete_reason_counts`, `pre_run_rejected`, `pre_run_cancelled`.
 - `completed_count == 0` ⇒ **insufficient evidence** (never a passing quality result).
 - A pre-run attempt records **no** `run_outcome`, creates **no** completed artifact, and is never counted as a started run.
 - Controlled before/after experiments carry `controlled_change` and are labelled as changed-factor comparisons; repeated fixed-condition benchmarks require matching controls. Exact scoring/threshold is C/A's (pending).

+## 13. Evidence and coverage model — `REQ-TA-FR-001/004/005/006` (PROPOSED, not implemented)
+
+Status: **proposed implementation-ready design** for D to build and C to test. Nothing here is implemented at `a62b801`; the existing run has **input provenance only** (`INV-04/05/05b`) and no per-run evidence or coverage record. This section is the **data contract** that the R2 (evidence-ID) and R7 (coverage-equality) check rules in §14 depend on; per the approved plan, this contract must be agreed **before** those checker integrations. Feasibility of implementing it before 25 Nov is **not promised** (see §16).
+
+### 13.1 Proposed components and module boundaries
+| Component | Responsibility | Proposed path (new) | Owner(design/impl/test/enforce) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `EvidenceRegistry` | Assign stable evidence IDs; retain per-item records; expose lookup for citation resolution | `tradingagents/runapi/evidence.py` | B / D / C / E |
+| `CoverageTracker` | Accumulate one code per channel; classify core/non-core; compute `NOT_REQUESTED`; render deterministic section | `tradingagents/runapi/coverage.py` | B / D / C / E |
+| Router/bypass seams | Emit a record/code for every channel, including the 2 router-bypass channels (3 and 11) | `tradingagents/dataflows/router.py` (+ bypass call sites) | B / D / C / E |
+
+Dependency rule preserved: `runapi/*` must not import `cli`.
+
+### 13.2 Field-level data contracts (authority noted per field)
+
+```
+EvidenceRecord {
+  evidence_id: str            # stable within a run; assigned by EvidenceRegistry (AUTHORITATIVE, deterministic)
+  channel: ChannelCode        # see §13.3 (deterministic)
+  source: str                 # vendor/source label as supplied (SOURCE-PROVIDED metadata; not model text)
+  ticker: str                 # instrument the item concerns (SOURCE-PROVIDED)
+  observed_at: str | null     # ISO-8601 when observed, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)
+  published_at: str | null    # ISO-8601 publication/filing date, else null (SOURCE-PROVIDED)
+  as_of_window: str           # the FR-004 window this item was admitted under (deterministic)
+  value_ref: str | null       # opaque pointer to the retained payload; NOT the payload text (deterministic)
+}
+```
+
+- **Invariant:** at least one of `observed_at` / `published_at` is non-null for every admitted item (R2 resolution depends on it). Enforced by `EvidenceRegistry` on admission.
+- **IDs are run-scoped** and never derived from model output. A citation in the rendered report references `evidence_id`; R2 (§14) resolves it against the registry.
+- **Retention vs outage:** records are written to the run's own artifact area. "Retain evidence after an ordinary engine failure" is **not** a promise that storage succeeds during a critical persistence outage; on critical report/manifest failure the run is `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` and no published paths are promised (§7.3). Evidence retention is best-effort relative to that critical boundary.
+
+```
+CoverageRecord {
+  channel: ChannelCode        # 12 channels (§13.3)
+  code: "OK" | "UNAVAILABLE" | "NO_DATA" | "STALE" | "WITHHELD" | "NOT_REQUESTED"   # (deterministic)
+  detail: str | null          # redacted, source-metadata-derived; never model prose
+}
+CoverageSet {
+  entries: CoverageRecord[12]         # exactly one row per channel (deterministic)
+  core_channels: ChannelCode[]        # e.g. price family; configurable, default per requirement
+  run_core_ok: bool                   # all core channels == OK
+}
+```
+
+- **Coverage is built from tool results, never written by the model.** The rendered "Data coverage" section is produced deterministically from `CoverageSet`; R7 (§14) asserts the rendered section equals the record.
+- `NOT_REQUESTED` = no selected analyst asked for this channel and no vendor call was made; valid for both COMPLETED and INCOMPLETE.
+- **Core rule:** any core channel ≠ `OK` ⇒ run ends `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`. Non-core gaps do not stop the run.
+
+### 13.3 Channel enumeration (12) and bypass handling
+Channels map to the router method map. **Channels 3 and 11 bypass the router** in the baseline and require explicit emission at their call sites (D must confirm the exact channel↔method mapping against `router.py` and the two bypass paths before implementation). The enum is a design proposal; the exact membership and the two bypass indices are **to be confirmed by D/C** against the real code (see §16 decision D5).
+
+### 13.4 Freshness (§`REQ-TA-FR-006`) — proposed parameters
+- Price freshness: latest bar ≤ `STALE_PRICE_DAYS` (10, fixed) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ core gap ⇒ `INCOMPLETE/DATA_FAILURE`.
+- Statement freshness: filed ≤ `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` (provisional, **open**) before *D*; exceeded ⇒ coded `STALE`, shown with filing date, run continues.
+- News/social: item inside the *D*-clamped window; excluded items are `NO_DATA`/`UNAVAILABLE`, not `STALE`.
+- `STALE_STATEMENT_DAYS` is a **configuration decision, not a measured value** (open; A owns).
+
+### 13.5 Normal sequence
+`admit(item) → assign evidence_id + record in EvidenceRegistry → set/refine CoverageRecord[channel]` for each retrieved item; at finalize, `coverage = CoverageSet.compute()` and `coverage.render()` produces the report section. Sequence integrates at the data boundary (`router`/bypass), before the checker runs.
+
+### 13.6 Failure / concurrency / privacy / persistence policy
+- **Failure:** a malformed item that cannot be admitted is a data error for that channel (coded), not a crash; core-gap ⇒ `DATA_FAILURE`.
+- **Concurrency:** analysts fan out; `EvidenceRegistry` and `CoverageTracker` mutations must be thread-safe (single lock per registry/tracker, or per-thread accumulation merged at join). IDs must remain unique under concurrency.
+- **Privacy:** records carry source metadata and an opaque `value_ref`, not raw payloads; redaction applies at any sink that emits records; holdings/other-position content never enters an evidence record.
+- **Persistence:** evidence/coverage are written into the run's artifact area; a critical publication failure does not promise their durability beyond §7.3; on ordinary engine failure, retained records stay available if storage worked.
+
+### 13.7 Compatibility/migration
+Additive fields only. Existing manifests gain `coverage` and (optionally) an evidence index reference; `schema_version` bumps. Old readers must tolerate the new fields (forward-compatible) or a version gate applies. No rename of existing `SafeRunMetadata` fields.
