+## 15A. Atomic call + token admission — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` (PROPOSED; Alt-B settlement)
+
+Status: **proposed implementation-ready design** for cumulative **token** admission, sitting **beside** the existing call-cap (§15), not replacing it. **Not implemented.** Alt-B chosen (known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention); see [ADR-004](adr/004-cumulative-token-admission.md). Mutable state is per-run and **outside** the frozen `RunContext`.
+
+### 15A.1 One atomic coordinator for both limits
+One per-run `AdmissionCoordinator` consults the call controller (§15) and the token controller **under one critical section**, withholding a grant from **both** if **either** limit refuses (no partial grant). It lives at the §15 controlled application client boundary (`tradingagents/llm_clients` dispatch seam; proposed `tradingagents/runapi/token_admission.py`). Integration with §15 is **targeted**: §15's counting rules are preserved; only the entry point is wrapped (§15.1 gains a cross-reference; see §15A.6).
+
+```
+Ticket { id; coordinator_run_id; call_grant; token_reservation; state: GRANTED|DISPATCHED|SETTLED_KNOWN|SETTLED_UNKNOWN|INVALIDATED }
+
+AdmissionCoordinator.admit(input_bound, output_allowance) -> Ticket
+  # atomic: (call grant ok) AND (K+R+U + input_bound + output_allowance <= TOKEN_BUDGET)
+  # if either refuses -> grant NEITHER; raise the refusing limit's typed error
+coordinate.dispatch(ticket)                     # GRANTED -> DISPATCHED, immediately BEFORE the provider request issues
+coordinate.settle_known(ticket, in_use, out_use)# DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_KNOWN
+coordinate.settle_unknown(ticket)               # DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_UNKNOWN
+coordinate.invalidate(ticket)                   # GRANTED -> INVALIDATED (unsent only; requires non-dispatch established)
+```
+
+### 15A.2 Defensible bounds vs estimates (required, not parameter choices)
+Reservation requires a **defensible upper bound**, not an estimate. Per enabled profile, the **provider/profile capability contract** must assert:
+- **Input upper bound** — an exact model tokenizer, **or** a tokenizer-family + safety multiplier that is **justified for the complete supported request domain**. Empirical samples alone do **not** prove an upper bound.
+- **Tool/schema overhead** — tool schemas, `bind_tools`, `with_structured_output` schema serialization and system-message overhead included in the input bound.
+- **Finite enforced output allowance** — a per-attempt maximum the client/provider **enforces** (e.g. forwarded `max_tokens`). `max_tokens=None` and advisory 450/220-word targets are **not** finite bounds.
+- **Request binding** — the reservation is bound to the **final prepared request + effective configuration**; the payload/config must not change after measurement (immutably referenced; a post-measurement mutation invalidates the ticket).
+
+A profile lacking any of these is **UNSUPPORTED**: token admission refuses to run for it and surfaces the decision; it is not silently estimated. Character/4 is **not** an admissible input bound. Numeric values (`TOKEN_BUDGET`, multiplier, output allowance) remain parameters; the **method + UNSUPPORTED behaviour do not**. Offline accounting tests verify the *accounting logic against a scripted provider*, **not** the deployed provider's true bounds.
+
+### 15A.3 One precise token ledger (mutually exclusive buckets)
+- **K** — known actual usage of **settled-known** attempts.
+- **R** — outstanding reservations for **granted/dispatched (in-flight)** attempts.
+- **U** — retained allowances for **UNKNOWN** attempts (held capacity; never reported as measured actual).
+
+**Admission:** `admit` iff `K + R + U + (input_bound + output_allowance) <= TOKEN_BUDGET`. **This invariant is conditional on the asserted request bounds holding**; a detected violation (§15A.4) is recorded and made visible, not hidden.
+
+**Held capacity** `H = K + R + U` is **not monotonic** (known settlement may reduce it). Keep **monotonic cumulative counters** separately: `cumulative_admitted`, `cumulative_consumed_known`.
+
+### 15A.4 Transitions (no double charge; violations recorded, never clamped)
+| Op | Precondition | Effect | Call counters (§15) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `admit` | call grant ok AND token fits | token reservation → **R** (full allowance); `cumulative_admitted += allowance` | `granted += 1` |
+| `dispatch` | ticket GRANTED | ticket → DISPATCHED (request issues next) | `dispatched += 1` |
+| `settle_known` | ticket DISPATCHED; **valid** input+output usage | remove allowance from **R**, add actual to **K**; `cumulative_consumed_known += actual`. H may decrease if actual < allowance | — |
+| `settle_known` with **actual > allowance** | ticket DISPATCHED | **Bound/protocol violation:** K += actual (full, **not clamped**), R -= allowance, record audit anomaly, **stop new admissions**, propagate typed `TokenBoundViolation` | — |
+| `settle_unknown` | ticket DISPATCHED; usage missing/partial | move allowance **R → U** (retained; **not** in K, not reported as actual) | — |
+| `invalidate` | ticket GRANTED; non-dispatch established | **release the complete token allowance** from **R** (returned to capacity); record invalidation | `invalidated += 1`; **`granted` stays `+1` permanently — the call grant is NOT refunded** |
+
+- **Settlement requires a DISPATCHED ticket.** Reuse, duplicate callbacks (settle twice), a non-dispatched settle, or **wrong-run** tickets raise `TokenProtocolError`, rejected **atomically**, with no bucket move.
+- **Dispatch/invalidation race:** exactly one of `DISPATCHED` or `INVALIDATED` per ticket; a second transition raises. If dispatch was issued, `invalidate` is refused (must settle).
+- **UNKNOWN resolution:** in this version **U stays until finalization; no late U→K**. (A future resolved-late path is out of scope here.)
+- **Token vs call invalidation are intentionally different:** token capacity **is** released on proven non-dispatch (no tokens spent); the **call** grant is **never** refunded (§15 monotonic admission). The coordinator does **not** refund call grants.
+- **Violation ≠ exhaustion:** `actual > allowance` is a bound/protocol violation that **may occur while total usage < TOKEN_BUDGET**; it is not budget exhaustion. It halts new admissions and is mapped per §15A.5.
+
+### 15A.5 Result mapping (no new serialized stop reason)
+- **Bound/protocol violation** → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` with a safe diagnostic naming the overage (budget kind, allowance, actual, ticket id; no prompts/secrets). Not `BUDGET` — total may be under budget.
+- **Ordinary refusal** of a *required* request that cannot fit → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=BUDGET`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`.
+- **`PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence** over both (critical report/manifest failure). **In-flight** attempts are accounted (R→K/U or recorded overage) before **immutable** finalization; a refused-required drop preserves partial content through normal publication. Single terminal, truthful durability; **no** new enum value.
+
+### 15A.6 Usage seam (capture before parsing discards the response)
+Usage is captured at the **model-request boundary**, immediately after the response returns and **before** structured parsing can discard it — including calls whose parsing then fails. Concretely (`tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py`, `agents/structured.py`): `NormalizedChatOpenAI.invoke`/`normalize_content` are **post-response** processing; `with_structured_output` **constructs a runnable** and issues no request; the request is `…invoke(...)`. The coordinator `dispatch`es before that `.invoke`, and reads `usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the returned response **before** `invoke_structured` may raise/fallback and drop it. **Known settlement requires valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ `settle_unknown`. Do **not** copy `cli/stats_handler.py`'s `.get(..., 0)` zero-default.
+
+### 15A.7 Compatibility / migration
+`schema_version` (result/manifest), `check_rules_version`, and the requirements JSON-Schema version are **separate axes** (§16.7). Add safe `run_budget`/token fields to `EffectiveConfig`+manifest (no prompts/secrets). Old readers **fail closed** on unknown version/fields. No new `StopReason` value. No application-format change merely because D1's schema changed.
+
+### 15A.8 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)
+| # | Scenario | Expected |
+|---|---|---|
+| T1 | reserve 60, settle known 20 (BUDGET 100) | R 60→0, K 20, H 20, remaining 80; calls granted 1, dispatched 1 |
+| T2 | reserve 60, settle UNKNOWN | R→U=60, K=0, H 60, remaining 40; UNKNOWN not reported as actual |
+| T3 | grant then invalidate unsent (CALL_CAP=1) | token fully released (H 0, remaining 100); calls granted 1, dispatched 0, invalidated 1; **next admit DENIED on call cap** |
+| T4 | four concurrent, remaining fits one | exactly 1 admit, 3 refused; K+R+U ≤ BUDGET; calls granted +1 |
+| T5 | duplicate settle / wrong-run / non-dispatched settle | `TokenProtocolError`, no bucket move |
+| T6 | actual (75) > allowance (60), total < budget | INTERNAL_ERROR (not BUDGET), K=75, overage visible, admissions halted, no clamp |
+| T7 | required request can't fit, total at budget | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET/NOT_RUN, no rating, findings [] |
+| T8 | violation + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary |
+| T9 | usage missing/partial | settle UNKNOWN, capacity retained |
+| T10 | old reader meets new field/version | fail closed |

 # Memory and State Design (Member B)
 
 Status: architecture draft (implementation-aligned 2026-11-24). Distinguishes pre-run cancellation, fresh started runs, transient state, immutable final artifacts, user-supplied portfolio data, provider transmission and retention/privacy. Named components exist in the `a62b801` checkout (verified); independent verification is C's. Resume changes are **deferred** in this selection and are **not** designed here (see §6 for the proposed D-5 conflict).
 
 ## 1. Lifecycle states
 
 | State | Meaning | Persisted? | LLM calls |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Pre-run cancellation/rejection | Discovered/cancelled/invalid input before consent, or consent declined | **No completed run**; no artifact; counted separately (NFR-006) | Zero |
 | Fresh started run | A new invocation after consent; gets a unique `run_id` | Transient during run; final artifacts after finalization | Yes |
 | Transient run state | In-memory graph state, message buffer, intermediate chunks | In-memory (plus existing log files) | — |
 | Immutable final artifacts | Final report (MD/HTML), manifest (published run directory) | **Yes, write-once** | — |
 | User-supplied portfolio data | Frozen snapshot from selected file | Held in `RunContext`; **not** written whole to new sinks | — |
 | Provider transmission | Holdings sent to configured model provider | Intentionally disclosed pre-consent as a notice; actual transmission **after** consent | Yes (during run) |
 | Retention/privacy | What persists locally and what is redacted | Per §4 | — |
 
 A fresh invocation always creates a fresh `run_id` (no resume in this selection).
 
 ## 2. Owned state
 - **`RunContext`** owns the immutable input identity (mode, frozen snapshot reference, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis, consent state). It is the authoritative provenance for report/result/manifest/check.
 - **Transient graph state** (`tradingagents/graph/propagation.py`, `agents/state.py`) carries rendered `portfolio_context` (string) to the decision agents — upstream behaviour preserved. The rendered string is derived once at run start (`trading_graph.py:293-307`).
 - **User-supplied portfolio data** is read **once**, validated, frozen; the file is never re-read after freeze (interface-contracts §4).
 
 ## 3. Write/retrieval policy
 - Each fresh run writes into its **own run-ID-isolated** location. Same-ticker/same-date runs must not overwrite a prior run's artifacts (INV-12); the legacy date-keyed state log (`full_states_log_{trade_date}.json`, `trading_graph.py:472`) is addressed in §5.
 - The manifest is written **atomically once** after artifact/check finalization, from the `SafeRunMetadata` projection — never the full `RunContext`/payload.
 - Retrieval for reads (e.g., console "where is my report") uses redacted paths; no secrets.
 - Resume: **deferred**. A final record is never mutated to simulate a resume.
 
 ## 4. Retention, retrieval and privacy (B3-09)
 
 - **Transient snapshot lifetime:** the frozen snapshot value tuples live only in `RunContext` for the duration of the process/run; they are **never written** to durable sinks and are released on process exit. No durable copy of holdings is created by this extension.
 - **Durable retention:** by default, artifacts persist under the run's isolated results directory **until the user deletes them**. This selection does **not** introduce automatic deletion or a cross-run catalogue (deferred). **Deletion owner:** the end user (application role); E/ops may define a later retention policy but must not silently delete user artifacts.
 - **Retrieval policy:** reads for provenance/console use the redacted `SafeInputMetadata`/`SafeRunMetadata`; the portfolio source file is not re-read after freeze; no full payload is retrieved from manifests/logs.
 - **Redaction ≠ suppression:** masking secrets (NFR-003) is **distinct** from suppressing raw holdings/prompt dumps. Both are required: raw portfolio bytes, full `RunContext`, raw provider prompts/payloads are **not persisted** in new sinks regardless of redaction.
 - **Provider retention:** holdings **transmitted to the provider after consent** are subject to the **provider's own retention/logging policy, outside application control**; the notice states this is intentional provider transmission. The application is not represented as local-only.
 - **Secrets:** never persisted; redaction boundary at every sink (§5).
 - **Source files:** portfolio source files are kept **read-only**; their bytes are not copied into manifests/transcripts.
 
 ## 5. Sink handling (existing + new)
 
 Each sink: decision (retain/adapt/disable/replace), output location, run-ID isolation, overwrite prevention, permitted content, redaction boundary, raw-payload suppression, failure handling, responsible component. Criticality and ordering are in `interface-contracts.md` §7.
 
 | Sink | Decision | Output location | Run-ID isolation & overwrite prevention | Permitted content | Redaction boundary | Raw payload suppression | Failure handling | Responsible component |
 |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
 | `message_tool.log` (`cli/run.py:139-164`) | **Adapt** | per-run results dir (`results_dir/<ticker>/<run_id>/message_tool.log`) | Under run-ID-isolated dir; never append across runs | Model/system narrative; no raw portfolio bytes/other-position dump | `Redactor` per line | Yes | **Best-effort:** failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip COMPLETED (not a promised artifact) | Persist + Redactor |
 | Graph state JSON `full_states_log_{trade_date}.json` (`trading_graph.py:472`) | **Adapt (replace path keying)** | per-run results dir | **Legacy date-keyed overwrites same ticker+date.** Replace with run-ID-qualified filename; refuse-if-exists | Existing narrative fields + safe provenance projection; never raw payload | `Redactor` on serialized entry | Yes | **Best-effort:** failure ⇒ redacted note; prior run preserved | Persist (path) + Redactor |
 | Markdown report (`reporting.py`) | **Adapt** | per-run dir (`reports/complete_report.md`) | Run-ID-qualified; **critical**: written to `_staging`, published only by the single directory commit (§interface-contracts §7); refuse silent overwrite | Checked body + trusted envelope from safe projection | Redact body **before** check; escape/redact provenance | Yes | **Critical:** staging/commit failure ⇒ INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR; no success exposed (§7) | reporting + Persist |
 | HTML report (`report_html.py`) | **Retain escaping, adapt provenance source** | alongside MD (`complete_report.html`) | Same as MD (critical when enabled) | Same checked body + escaped envelope | Already escapes (`:10,226,255`); extend to provenance | Yes | Same as MD | reporting + Persist |
 | **Manifest (new)** | **New** | per-run dir (`manifest.json`) | Run-ID-qualified; **written into `_staging` before the single commit**; immutable after commit; refuse overwrite | `Manifest` (`SafeRunMetadata` + paths + `terminal_event.durable`, decided pre-commit); **no payload/secret endpoints** | `Redactor` before staging write | Yes | **Critical:** staging/commit failure ⇒ INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR; nothing published | Persist |
 | **JSONL event sink (new)** | **New** | per-run dir (`events.jsonl`) | Run-ID-qualified; **terminal event appended to `_staging` before commit (sets `durable`)**; other progress events best-effort | Fixed fields (§interface-contracts §3.9) | `Redactor` per event | Yes | **Best-effort, non-critical: terminal append failure ⇒ `terminal_event.durable=false` (manifest states it) but the logical outcome is preserved and the run is published; progress-event failure ⇒ redacted note, never changes the immutable manifest** | EventSink + Persist |
 
 **Disclosure distinction:** decision-agent narrative necessarily receives provider-summarized context **after consent** (intentional disclosure). This is distinct from copying **raw portfolio bytes / full provider payloads** into manifests/logs/events/state JSON, which is prohibited (INV-06).
 
 ## 6. Non-goals
 No resume/checkpoint redesign, no cross-run catalogue, no aggregate budget persistence. Upstream checkpoint fingerprint (12-char) remains a checkpoint concern, preserved unchanged.
 
 ## 7. Proposed broader changes — impact, not implemented (2026-11-24)
 
 - **Aggregate budgets (`REQ-TA-NFR-PERF-002`, `COST-001/002`, `BUDGET`):** if adopted, a run-scoped budget controller and a sixth `stop_reason` would be added; neither exists in `runapi/result.py` today. This section does **not** design or adopt it.
 - **Resume identity (D-5 proposal):** the candidate suggests a resumed run keeps its `run_id` and appends an attempt, whereas this design gives **every fresh invocation a fresh `run_id`** and treats final records as immutable (INV-11/INV-12). These **conflict**; adoption would be a separate contract change (OQ-8), not implied by the current selection. Not implemented.
 - **Per-run coverage/evidence records (`REQ-TA-FR-001/005`):** would add durable per-run coverage and evidence registries. The as-built sinks (§5) do not persist these; only input provenance is durable.
 
 ## 8. Run-budget controller state (proposed; not implemented)
 
 The `RunBudgetController` (interface-contracts §15) holds **mutable per-run budget state** (reservation/counter state per slot). This state:
 - is **separate from the frozen input snapshot** (`RunContext` is immutable and not touched by the budget);
 - is **one per run** and never a global counter shared across unrelated runs;
 - is not persisted as part of the immutable manifest beyond safe audit counts (cap, attempts, reservations, denials); no prompts/secrets are retained.
 
 **Resume identity remains a separate, undecided contract** (ADR 002 D5): this selection uses a fresh `run_id` per invocation (INV-12) and immutable artifacts; a logical-run + attempt model is **not** adopted here and does not conflict-resolve automatically. Interruption (`INTERRUPTED`) semantics are unchanged and do not themselves settle resume.
 
-## 9. Intermediate context assembly and rollback — concise mode (feature `9102759`; pending integration)
+## 9. Intermediate context assembly and rollback — concise mode (integrated at `adb4dfc`, PR #18)
 
-Status: describes behaviour **implemented on feature branch `9102759caaa59d778ba49cd57a1306f5f2ee5d88` (PR #18), not yet on main**. It bears on this document's owned state (prompt/context assembly) but does not alter retention/privacy or the input-snapshot contracts.
+Status: describes behaviour **integrated into main via PR #18 (merge `adb4dfc`, ancestor of current HEAD)**; the dangling-reference boundary and quality acceptance remain open. It bears on this document's owned state (prompt/context assembly) but does not alter retention/privacy or the input-snapshot contracts.
 
 - **Assembly location.** Intermediate analyst and debate prompts are assembled in `agents/analysts/turn.py` and the Bull/Bear/risk agents during the analysis-execution stage (blueprint §5 step 6). Concise mode's brevity guidance is appended to the **assembled system message** in the analyst tool loop (`turn.py`) but to the **assembled prompt strings** in the Bull/Bear researchers and risk debaters; a duplicated opponent argument may additionally be replaced with a reference.
 - **Exact reference, not semantic dedup.** A reference is emitted only when the exact stripped opponent text already occurs in debate history; otherwise the explicit copy is kept. This is **exact Python string-substring matching**, not summarization.
 - **Restore-before-guard.** `bound_debate_prompt` reconstructs the explicit copies before invoking the existing `bound_agent_prompt` guard when the reconstructed-original length would exceed `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens) * 4`. The trusted `<protected_context>` portfolio block is unaffected and remains protected by the guard. **No unconditional no-dangling guarantee:** a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so a reference-form prompt longer than the restored original can still be compacted and lose its cited history (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Restoring a copy before the guard is **not** a promise that all narrative survives compaction.
 - **No new forced truncation.** The feature adds no truncation of generated output or tool payloads; the pre-existing character/4 prompt guard can still trim narrative.
 - **Trusted facts preserved.** Prompt guidance is **advisory** and cannot change authoritative provenance, check results, or the protected portfolio facts; it is not deterministic semantic enforcement.
 - **Effective configuration and rollback.** `concise_intermediate_reports` defaults to `True`; `TRADINGAGENTS_CONCISE_INTERMEDIATE_REPORTS=false` (or programmatic `False`) restores legacy verbosity for a new process. The flag is recorded in `run_settings()`/`EffectiveConfig` (interface-contracts §3.7) and is **not** part of `prompt_hash`; the touched prompt source files are (§3.8), so new runs' `prompt_hash` differs from pre-feature runs.
 - **Legacy artifacts.** An existing run record that lacks `concise_intermediate_reports` is **legacy/unknown mode**, not today's `True` default and not `False`; historical runs are not relabeled.
 - **Separation from budgets.** This is not the existing per-prompt guard contract change and not ADR-002's proposed run-wide `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (Slice C, unimplemented). Observed token savings do not satisfy `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`.
+
+## 10. Cumulative token-admission state (proposed; not implemented)
+
+The token-admission controller (interface-contracts §15A, ADR-004, Alt-B) holds **mutable per-run ledger state** — buckets K (known actual), R (reserved/in-flight), U (UNKNOWN retained), plus monotonic `cumulative_admitted`/`cumulative_consumed_known` and the held tickets. This state:
+- is **separate from the frozen input snapshot** (`RunContext` is immutable and never carries budget counters);
+- is **one per run** (coordinated with the §15 call cap through `AdmissionCoordinator`), never a global counter shared across runs;
+- is **not persisted** in the immutable manifest beyond safe audit counts (`K/R/U`, budget, denied/violation flags) — no prompts/secrets;
+- **does not** resolve UNKNOWN late: `U` remains until finalization in this version (no `U→K` conversion), and a bound/protocol violation is recorded truthfully (never clamped), not hidden inside the manifest.
+
+**Independence preserved:** this is distinct from the existing per-prompt character/4 guard and the concise-context feature (ADR-003); it is the run-wide cumulative-token design that sits beside ADR-002's call-cap (§15), not a replacement for it.

Approve Phase 2 documentation drafting using Alt-B: known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention. Apply these resolutions consistently before describing the design as implementation-ready:

1. **Correct invalidation accounting**
After granting and then invalidating an unsent ticket:
- token reservation is fully released;
- calls granted = 1, dispatched = 0, invalidated = 1;
- the call grant remains charged permanently.
At CALL_CAP=1, another admission is denied even though token capacity was restored. Remove every suggestion that the coordinator refunds call grants.

2. **Separate bound violation from budget exhaustion**
Actual usage above its reservation is a bound/protocol violation; it may occur while total usage remains below TOKEN_BUDGET. Record actual usage without clamping, immediately stop new admissions and propagate a typed violation through the broad handlers.

For this proposed design, map a bound/protocol violation to INTERNAL_ERROR with a safe diagnostic; ordinary refusal of a required request maps to BUDGET. Account for in-flight work before immutable finalization. Preserve PERSISTENCE_ERROR precedence, incomplete NOT_RUN and empty checker findings. Do not introduce a new serialized stop reason.

3. **Finish the state contract**
Define explicit joint-ticket grant, dispatch, known settlement, UNKNOWN settlement and pre-dispatch invalidation operations. Settlement requires a dispatched ticket. Reject reuse, duplicate callbacks and wrong-run operations atomically.

For this version, UNKNOWN remains in U until finalization; do not introduce late U→K resolution. State explicitly that K+R+U≤budget is conditional on the asserted request bounds holding; a detected violation must remain visible.

4. **Make the alternatives genuinely different**
Alt-A permanently charges the full dispatched allowance even after smaller known usage, while recording measured usage separately. Alt-B releases unused allowance after known settlement and retains UNKNOWN capacity. Compare their tradeoffs as current design reasoning, not measured experiments. Select Alt-B.

5. **Use defensible bounds and correct usage seams**
A tokenizer-family multiplier is eligible only with justification for the complete supported request domain; empirical samples alone do not prove an upper bound. Unsupported profiles remain explicitly unsupported.

Admission must occur before the actual provider request. Capture usage before structured parsing can discard the raw response, including calls whose parsing fails. normalize_content is post-response processing; with_structured_output constructs a runnable rather than itself issuing a request.

Require valid input and output usage for known settlement. Missing/partial usage becomes UNKNOWN; do not copy the CLI callback’s zero-default behavior.

6. **Complete the approved documentation scope**
Include the metadata-only docs/req/README.md update and targeted §15 coordinator integration references. Preserve C2, ADR-002’s call-count semantics and ADR-003’s Proposed decision status. Record integration separately. COST-001’s wording cleanup is resolved at HEAD 5672a79.

No application, tests, canonical requirements, CI, evidence or logs may change. No live calls, commits or pushes. Finish with source/interface/scenario mappings, checks and remaining deployment prerequisites, then stop for review.
I'll verify the remaining seams before drafting, then write the Phase 2 documents with Alt-B and your six resolutions applied consistently.

import logging
import os
import re
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

from .api_key_env import get_api_key_env
from .base_client import BaseLLMClient, normalize_content
from .capabilities import get_capabilities
from .validators import validate_model

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class NormalizedChatOpenAI(ChatOpenAI):
    """ChatOpenAI with normalized content output and capability-aware binding.

    The Responses API returns content as a list of typed blocks
    (reasoning, text, etc.). ``invoke`` normalizes to string for
    consistent downstream handling.

    ``with_structured_output`` consults the per-model capability table
    (``capabilities.get_capabilities``) to pick the method and to decide
    whether ``tool_choice`` may be sent. Models that reject ``tool_choice``
    (e.g. DeepSeek V4 and reasoner — per their official tool-calling
    guide) still bind the schema as a tool, but no ``tool_choice``
    parameter is sent.

    Provider-specific quirks beyond structured-output (e.g. DeepSeek's
    reasoning_content roundtrip) live in subclasses so this base class
    stays small.
    """

    def invoke(self, input, config=None, **kwargs):
        return normalize_content(super().invoke(input, config, **kwargs))

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, *, method=None, **kwargs):
        caps = get_capabilities(self.model_name)
        if caps.preferred_structured_method == "none":
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"{self.model_name} has no structured-output method available; "
                f"agent factories will fall back to free-text generation."
            )
        method = method or caps.preferred_structured_method
        # When the model rejects tool_choice, suppress langchain's hardcoded
        # value. The schema is still bound as a tool — exactly what
        # DeepSeek's official tool-calling examples do.
        if method == "function_calling" and not caps.supports_tool_choice:
            kwargs.setdefault("tool_choice", None)
        return super().with_structured_output(schema, method=method, **kwargs)


class LocalCompatibleChatOpenAI(NormalizedChatOpenAI):
    """OpenAI-compatible client for arbitrary local servers (LM Studio, vLLM,
    llama.cpp via the generic ``openai_compatible`` provider).
=== structured parse path ===
NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (
    "Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools "
    "or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly."
)


def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:
    """Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.

    Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent
    will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.
    """
    try:
        return llm.with_structured_output(schema)
    except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:
        logger.warning(
            "%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); "
            "falling back to free-text generation",
            agent_name, _diagnostic(exc),
        )
        return None


def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:
    """Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.

    ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat
    invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that
    shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.
    """
    if structured_llm is None:
        return None
    prompt = bound_agent_prompt(prompt)
    try:
        result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)
        if result is None:
            # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling
            # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it
            # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.
            raise ValueError("structured output returned no parsed result")
        return result
    except ContextBudgetError:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning(
            "%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text",
            agent_name, _diagnostic(exc),
        )
        return None


def invoke_structured_or_freetext(
    structured_llm: Any | None,
    plain_llm: Any,
    prompt: Any,
    render: Callable[[T], str],
    agent_name: str,
) -> str:
    """Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure."""
    prompt = bound_agent_prompt(prompt)
    result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)
    if result is not None:
        return render(result)
    return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content

    def on_llm_end(self, response: LLMResult, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Extract token usage from LLM response."""
        try:
            generation = response.generations[0][0]
        except (IndexError, TypeError):
            return

        usage_metadata = None
        if hasattr(generation, "message"):

            if isinstance(message, AIMessage) and hasattr(message, "usage_metadata"):

---

## 15A. Atomic call + token admission — `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` (PROPOSED; Alt-B settlement)

Status: **proposed implementation-ready design** for cumulative **token** admission, sitting **beside** the existing call-cap (§15), not replacing it. **Not implemented.** Alt-B chosen (known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention); see [ADR-004](adr/004-cumulative-token-admission.md). Mutable state is per-run and **outside** the frozen `RunContext`.

### 15A.1 One atomic coordinator for both limits
One per-run `AdmissionCoordinator` consults the call controller (§15) and the token controller **under one critical section**, withholding a grant from **both** if **either** limit refuses (no partial grant). It lives at the §15 controlled application client boundary (`tradingagents/llm_clients` dispatch seam; proposed `tradingagents/runapi/token_admission.py`). Integration with §15 is **targeted**: §15's counting rules are preserved; only the entry point is wrapped (§15.1 gains a cross-reference; see §15A.6).

```
Ticket { id; coordinator_run_id; call_grant; token_reservation; state: GRANTED|DISPATCHED|SETTLED_KNOWN|SETTLED_UNKNOWN|INVALIDATED }

AdmissionCoordinator.admit(input_bound, output_allowance) -> Ticket
  # atomic: (call grant ok) AND (K+R+U + input_bound + output_allowance <= TOKEN_BUDGET)
  # if either refuses -> grant NEITHER; raise the refusing limit's typed error
coordinate.dispatch(ticket)                     # GRANTED -> DISPATCHED, immediately BEFORE the provider request issues
coordinate.settle_known(ticket, in_use, out_use)# DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_KNOWN
coordinate.settle_unknown(ticket)               # DISPATCHED -> SETTLED_UNKNOWN
coordinate.invalidate(ticket)                   # GRANTED -> INVALIDATED (unsent only; requires non-dispatch established)
```

### 15A.2 Defensible bounds vs estimates (required, not parameter choices)
Reservation requires a **defensible upper bound**, not an estimate. Per enabled profile, the **provider/profile capability contract** must assert:
- **Input upper bound** — an exact model tokenizer, **or** a tokenizer-family + safety multiplier that is **justified for the complete supported request domain**. Empirical samples alone do **not** prove an upper bound.
- **Tool/schema overhead** — tool schemas, `bind_tools`, `with_structured_output` schema serialization and system-message overhead included in the input bound.
- **Finite enforced output allowance** — a per-attempt maximum the client/provider **enforces** (e.g. forwarded `max_tokens`). `max_tokens=None` and advisory 450/220-word targets are **not** finite bounds.
- **Request binding** — the reservation is bound to the **final prepared request + effective configuration**; the payload/config must not change after measurement (immutably referenced; a post-measurement mutation invalidates the ticket).

A profile lacking any of these is **UNSUPPORTED**: token admission refuses to run for it and surfaces the decision; it is not silently estimated. Character/4 is **not** an admissible input bound. Numeric values (`TOKEN_BUDGET`, multiplier, output allowance) remain parameters; the **method + UNSUPPORTED behaviour do not**. Offline accounting tests verify the *accounting logic against a scripted provider*, **not** the deployed provider's true bounds.

### 15A.3 One precise token ledger (mutually exclusive buckets)
- **K** — known actual usage of **settled-known** attempts.
- **R** — outstanding reservations for **granted/dispatched (in-flight)** attempts.
- **U** — retained allowances for **UNKNOWN** attempts (held capacity; never reported as measured actual).

**Admission:** `admit` iff `K + R + U + (input_bound + output_allowance) <= TOKEN_BUDGET`. **This invariant is conditional on the asserted request bounds holding**; a detected violation (§15A.4) is recorded and made visible, not hidden.

**Held capacity** `H = K + R + U` is **not monotonic** (known settlement may reduce it). Keep **monotonic cumulative counters** separately: `cumulative_admitted`, `cumulative_consumed_known`.

### 15A.4 Transitions (no double charge; violations recorded, never clamped)
| Op | Precondition | Effect | Call counters (§15) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admit` | call grant ok AND token fits | token reservation → **R** (full allowance); `cumulative_admitted += allowance` | `granted += 1` |
| `dispatch` | ticket GRANTED | ticket → DISPATCHED (request issues next) | `dispatched += 1` |
| `settle_known` | ticket DISPATCHED; **valid** input+output usage | remove allowance from **R**, add actual to **K**; `cumulative_consumed_known += actual`. H may decrease if actual < allowance | — |
| `settle_known` with **actual > allowance** | ticket DISPATCHED | **Bound/protocol violation:** K += actual (full, **not clamped**), R -= allowance, record audit anomaly, **stop new admissions**, propagate typed `TokenBoundViolation` | — |
| `settle_unknown` | ticket DISPATCHED; usage missing/partial | move allowance **R → U** (retained; **not** in K, not reported as actual) | — |
| `invalidate` | ticket GRANTED; non-dispatch established | **release the complete token allowance** from **R** (returned to capacity); record invalidation | `invalidated += 1`; **`granted` stays `+1` permanently — the call grant is NOT refunded** |

- **Settlement requires a DISPATCHED ticket.** Reuse, duplicate callbacks (settle twice), a non-dispatched settle, or **wrong-run** tickets raise `TokenProtocolError`, rejected **atomically**, with no bucket move.
- **Dispatch/invalidation race:** exactly one of `DISPATCHED` or `INVALIDATED` per ticket; a second transition raises. If dispatch was issued, `invalidate` is refused (must settle).
- **UNKNOWN resolution:** in this version **U stays until finalization; no late U→K**. (A future resolved-late path is out of scope here.)
- **Token vs call invalidation are intentionally different:** token capacity **is** released on proven non-dispatch (no tokens spent); the **call** grant is **never** refunded (§15 monotonic admission). The coordinator does **not** refund call grants.
- **Violation ≠ exhaustion:** `actual > allowance` is a bound/protocol violation that **may occur while total usage < TOKEN_BUDGET**; it is not budget exhaustion. It halts new admissions and is mapped per §15A.5.

### 15A.5 Result mapping (no new serialized stop reason)
- **Bound/protocol violation** → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=INTERNAL_ERROR` with a safe diagnostic naming the overage (budget kind, allowance, actual, ticket id; no prompts/secrets). Not `BUDGET` — total may be under budget.
- **Ordinary refusal** of a *required* request that cannot fit → `INCOMPLETE` / `stop_reason=BUDGET`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`.
- **`PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence** over both (critical report/manifest failure). **In-flight** attempts are accounted (R→K/U or recorded overage) before **immutable** finalization; a refused-required drop preserves partial content through normal publication. Single terminal, truthful durability; **no** new enum value.

### 15A.6 Usage seam (capture before parsing discards the response)
Usage is captured at the **model-request boundary**, immediately after the response returns and **before** structured parsing can discard it — including calls whose parsing then fails. Concretely (`tradingagents/llm_clients/openai_client.py`, `agents/structured.py`): `NormalizedChatOpenAI.invoke`/`normalize_content` are **post-response** processing; `with_structured_output` **constructs a runnable** and issues no request; the request is `…invoke(...)`. The coordinator `dispatch`es before that `.invoke`, and reads `usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the returned response **before** `invoke_structured` may raise/fallback and drop it. **Known settlement requires valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ `settle_unknown`. Do **not** copy `cli/stats_handler.py`'s `.get(..., 0)` zero-default.

### 15A.7 Compatibility / migration
`schema_version` (result/manifest), `check_rules_version`, and the requirements JSON-Schema version are **separate axes** (§16.7). Add safe `run_budget`/token fields to `EffectiveConfig`+manifest (no prompts/secrets). Old readers **fail closed** on unknown version/fields. No new `StopReason` value. No application-format change merely because D1's schema changed.

### 15A.8 Proposed verification scenarios (C inputs; not accepted)
| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | reserve 60, settle known 20 (BUDGET 100) | R 60→0, K 20, H 20, remaining 80; calls granted 1, dispatched 1 |
| T2 | reserve 60, settle UNKNOWN | R→U=60, K=0, H 60, remaining 40; UNKNOWN not reported as actual |
| T3 | grant then invalidate unsent (CALL_CAP=1) | token fully released (H 0, remaining 100); calls granted 1, dispatched 0, invalidated 1; **next admit DENIED on call cap** |
| T4 | four concurrent, remaining fits one | exactly 1 admit, 3 refused; K+R+U ≤ BUDGET; calls granted +1 |
| T5 | duplicate settle / wrong-run / non-dispatched settle | `TokenProtocolError`, no bucket move |
| T6 | actual (75) > allowance (60), total < budget | INTERNAL_ERROR (not BUDGET), K=75, overage visible, admissions halted, no clamp |
| T7 | required request can't fit, total at budget | INCOMPLETE/BUDGET/NOT_RUN, no rating, findings [] |
| T8 | violation + critical persistence failure | PERSISTENCE_ERROR primary |
| T9 | usage missing/partial | settle UNKNOWN, capacity retained |
| T10 | old reader meets new field/version | fail closed |
S15A_EOF

input.content:
# ADR 004 — Cumulative token admission beside the call cap (Alt-B settlement)

- Status: **Proposed (architecture record 2026-11-24)**. A genuinely new design cycle for `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` (cumulative token budget). It **does not modify** the C2 evaluation (C1/C2/C3) in [ADR 001](001-portfolio-aware-cli.md), the call-cap design (ADR-002 D3, §15), or the concise-context record (ADR-003, still **Proposed**). Not implementation; D implementation and C acceptance pending.
- Deciders: Member B (author), pending A (requirement meaning), C (verification), D (feasibility), E (evidence). Does not adopt requirements.
- Scope: cumulative input+output token admission across all model-request paths, alongside §15's call cap. Detailed contracts: [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §15A; state: [memory-design.md](../memory-design.md) §10.

> This is current design reasoning, not a measured experiment. No paid runs, no invented comparison.

## Context

§15 bounds the **number** of model-request attempts (`CALL_CAP`) with monotonic, single-use call reservations. That is orthogonal to **token** consumption: a within-cap run can still spend unbounded tokens (long prompts, large outputs, retries, concurrency). `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` requires a cumulative input+output budget with **reserve-before-dispatch**. `max_tokens=None` and the advisory 450/220-word targets are **not** finite output bounds. The provider-usage seam exists (`usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`) but `cli/stats_handler.py` zero-defaults missing fields, which must not be copied.

## Decision

Adopt, as a **proposed** design, a per-run `AdmissionCoordinator` that checks the §15 call cap **and** a token ledger **atomically** (no partial grant), with these elements:

1. **Defensible bounds, not estimates.** Admission requires a per-profile provider capability contract: a defensible **input upper bound** (exact tokenizer, or tokenizer-family + safety multiplier **justified for the complete supported request domain**; samples alone do not prove an upper bound), **tool/schema overhead** included, and a **finite enforced output allowance**. A profile lacking these is **UNSUPPORTED** (admission refuses; surfaced as a decision), never silently estimated. Character/4 is not admissible. The reservation is bound to the **final prepared request + config**, immutable after measurement.
2. **Mutually exclusive ledger** K (known actual) / R (reserved/in-flight) / U (UNKNOWN retained). Admission: `K+R+U+(input_bound+output_allowance) <= TOKEN_BUDGET` **conditional on the bounds holding**; a violation is made visible, never hidden. `H=K+R+U` is **not** monotonic; cumulative counters are.
3. **Alt-B settlement:** on **known** usage, move R→K with actual (unused allowance released; a decrease in H is intended); on **UNKNOWN**, move R→U (capacity retained, not reported as actual). **This version keeps U until finalization — no late U→K.**
4. **Invariant/refusal/overage semantics:** a **bound/protocol violation** (actual > allowance) records actual (no clamp), halts admissions, propagates a typed `TokenBoundViolation` → `INTERNAL_ERROR` with a safe diagnostic; an **ordinary required-refusal** (cannot fit) → `BUDGET`. **No new serialized stop reason.** `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence preserved; in-flight accounted before immutable finalization; single terminal; truthful durability.
5. **Usage seam correctness:** admission happens **before** the provider request; usage is captured from the returned response **before** structured parsing can discard it (including parse-failure paths). `normalize_content` is post-response; `with_structured_output` builds a runnable and issues no request; notify-dispatch occurs at the real `.invoke`. Known settlement requires **valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ UNKNOWN.
6. **Call-cap coordination:** one atomic ticket; call grants are **never refunded** on invalidation (§15 monotonic), while **token** capacity **is** released on proven non-dispatch. Integration is a **targeted wrapper** of §15's entry point; §15 counting rules unchanged.

## Alternatives (genuinely distinct; current reasoning)

- **Alt-A — conservative full-allowance retention.** A dispatched attempt **permanently charges its full allowance** even if known usage is smaller; measured usage is recorded **separately** as information. Simplest accounting; strictest (persistently under-admits after cheap calls); UNKNOWN is a non-issue since the allowance was never released.
- **Alt-B — known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention (SELECTED).** On known settle, release unused allowance (R→K by actual); on UNKNOWN, retain capacity in U. Tighter capacity use; requires reliable usage capture + explicit UNKNOWN handling. **Selected** because it better matches `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001`'s intent (count actual cumulative tokens, not permanently over-charge) while still reserving-before-dispatch and retaining UNKNOWN.
- **Usage-only post-accounting (NON-COMPLIANT).** Admit *after* observing usage. Cannot reserve before dispatch and cannot bound concurrency; explicitly **not compliant** with COST-001. Not offered as a choice.

**Tradeoff of the selection:** Alt-B's accuracy depends on the usage seam and bounds holding; a bound/protocol violation must be surfaced (it is). Alt-B is not "uniquely compliant" versus Alt-A — both reserve before dispatch and satisfy the reserve clause; Alt-A is more conservative and simpler, Alt-B uses capacity more efficiently. The choice reflects the requirement's "count actual tokens" intent, not a measured result.

## Consequences
- **Positive:** a checkable cumulative bound with a precise ledger; violations visible; no new stop reason; §15 call semantics preserved; reversible/parked behind a config gate.
- **Costs/limits:** requires the provider/profile bounds contract (UNSUPPORTED otherwise); bound violation may occur even under budget → `INTERNAL_ERROR`; empirical per-profile bound validity is separate evidence (E). Offline tests prove accounting logic, not deployed bounds. U retained to finalization (no late resolution) may overstate held capacity.
- **Preserved:** C2 history; ADR-002 call semantics; ADR-003 Proposed status; no adoption of `TOKEN_BUDGET`/`CALL_CAP`/120000.

## Related
- Canonical blueprint: [../../../architecture-blueprint.md](../../../architecture-blueprint.md)
- [../interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §15 (call cap), §15A (token admission), §16.7 (version axes) · [../invariants.md](../invariants.md) INV-18/INV-20 · [../runtime-policy-catalog.md](../runtime-policy-catalog.md) R17/R23/R24 · [../memory-design.md](../memory-design.md) §10

 ## 8A. Engineering contributions (project-specific design)
 
 This section states the team's concrete engineering contributions honestly. The individual mechanisms are **standard software-engineering techniques** (immutability, content hashing, atomic directory replacement, append-before-dispatch ledgers, fail-closed checks). We do **not** claim to have invented them, and a standard technique's use does not by itself establish originality. The contribution is the **problem-specific design, its adaptation across the existing TradingAgents pipeline, and the demonstrated effect** in this application; the professor assesses originality. Each item separates what is **deterministically enforced** from what depends on **model compliance** (pending semantic acceptance).
 
 ### 8A.1 Protected portfolio facts across Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager
 
 - **Concrete problem.** In the baseline the portfolio block reached some decision stages unevenly. A real observed failure (2026-11-18, F9) showed an explicit-empty `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` run completing with deterministic check `PASSED` while the Trader/Portfolio-Manager narrative still spoke of "reducing/retaining existing exposure" — an unsupported account claim. Downstream stages could also inherit an ownership premise asserted upstream (the Research Manager's investment plan) without access to the same supplied facts.
 - **Design decision.** Route the same protected portfolio block through a single helper, `get_portfolio_context_from_state` (`tradingagents/agents/context.py:214`), into **all three** decision stages — Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager — and wrap it in `<protected_context>…</protected_context>` (`protect_context`, `context.py:271`) so context compaction cannot drop it. Absent input yields an explicit "no account ownership is assumed / unknown, not flat" notice; explicit-empty carries a no-nonzero-target instruction; a held book carries the supplied quantity. The stage instruction tells the model to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises (R4). The five research ratings and three Trader actions are unchanged; no rating is forced.
 - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R4 repair (2026-11-21): equalized the block across all three stages and added the corrective instruction. It is a prompt-grounding change, **not** a new authoritative check.
 - **Tradeoff.** Prompt text grows slightly and each stage must be kept consistent; grounding reduces but cannot eliminate unsupported narrative. A deterministic ownership check would be a larger change the current Q1–Q4 checker deliberately does not make.
 - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (R4). **Deterministically enforced:** the trusted facts are delivered to all three stages and survive compaction (prompt-capture tests). **Not enforced deterministically:** that the model's prose never asserts an unsupported position — that is assessed semantically (pending C, GOV-004).
 - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r4_research_manager_context.py` (RM/Trader/PM prompt distinction, shared facts, user-supplied/unverified label surviving compaction, absent≠flat); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr004_propagation.py`, `test_fr005_ratings.py`. Source: `tradingagents/agents/managers/research_manager.py:27-52`, `portfolio_manager.py:30-51`, `trader/trader.py:34,82-93`, `context.py:214-273`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json`; `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.
 - **Residual limitation.** Prompts cannot guarantee every future narrative; Q1–Q4 does not inspect ownership wording. The concrete demonstration is the **explicit-empty → upstream RM trim error the downstream stages corrected → protected-context repair → fresh RM/Trader/PM prompt evidence** thread recorded in the remediation review (retained diagnostics, not a new experiment run here).
 
 ### 8A.2 Separation of model advice from authoritative provenance/check results (truthful publication and failure handling)
 
 - **Concrete problem.** Model narrative, ratings text and any self-claimed "OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED" are advisory but can be mistaken for authoritative state; and a run can claim success while its artifacts failed to publish, or leave a caller-visible COMPLETED terminal for an unpublished run.
 - **Design decision.** Advisory model output is separated from authoritative, deterministic state:
   - **Provenance** is built only from the frozen `RunContext` and a full 64-char SHA-256 over canonical JSON bytes (`runapi/context.py`), never re-read from the file or `final_state`.
   - **Check authority** lives in one non-LLM `OutputChecker` (Q1–Q4); model text cannot set or override `output_check` (`runapi/checks.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py::test_tc_fr007_c_model_claim_cannot_override`).
   - **Outcome** is decided by `OutcomeFinalizer` from typed exceptions (`runapi/finalize.py`).
   - **Truthful publication:** report+manifest are **critical** and published by a **single atomic directory rename**; the JSONL terminal event is **best-effort** and its real durability is recorded as `terminal_event.durable` before the immutable manifest is staged (`runapi/persist.py:130-157`). A critical staging/commit failure returns `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` with no artifact promise. A tentative terminal is staged privately and revealed only after the commit; a post-commit callback failure cannot revise a published COMPLETED result (R5).
 - **Baseline/team change.** Bounded R5 repair plus the C2 boundary (`runapi/` modules). These separate advisory from authoritative status and make publication truthfully conditional.
 - **Tradeoff.** More modules and a staging directory; best-effort events mean a run can publish with `durable=false` (stated, not hidden). Not a power-loss durability guarantee.
 - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** (Q1–Q4 + R5). **Deterministically enforced:** check authority, provenance identity, conditional result fields, single-commit publication, truthful `durable`. **Residual:** the checker only covers Q1–Q4, not factual accuracy; terminal append remains best-effort.
 - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (rename-failure exposes INCOMPLETE only, manifest-write consistency, terminal-append keeps logical outcome, tentative not exposed pre-commit, single terminal); C seams `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_fr006_provenance.py`, `test_fr007_output_check.py`, `test_nfr004_persistence.py`, `test_nfr002_events.py`. Source: `runapi/checks.py`, `runapi/finalize.py`, `runapi/persist.py`, `runapi/events.py`, `runapi/reporting.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md`.
 - **Residual limitation.** Q1–Q4 certifies only its named rules, not truth or account suitability; publication durability is cooperative, not power-loss-proof. Demonstration: the **publication-failure / counterfeit-terminal negatives** in `test_r5_terminal_visibility.py` (offline regression material, not a new live run).
 
 ### 8A.3 Evaluation-evidence integrity (case/config/artifact correspondence, counterfeit rejection, unsuccessful-attempt accounting)
 - **Concrete problem.** A semantic score is only meaningful if each result is bound to the case, configuration and artifact it claims to have come from; a forged or mismatched artifact could otherwise pass, and silently dropping failed or incomplete attempts could inflate completion/quality.
 - **Design decision.** The live scorer/harness (`tests/member_c_verification/live/`) enforces the points below. **Provenance, by verified commit (roles only):** the evaluator originated as Member C's supplied tooling (`f66fc14`, `57b164c`, `b8c4a25`); it was subsequently hardened (`bb777d5`); the R2/R3 correspondence/counterfeit-replay repairs and the `tests/member_b_remediation/` regression tests were made in the supervised OpenCode repair session under a Brian-approved plan (`56bbe29`). `replay_store.py` was introduced in `56bbe29`, **not** with the original evaluator. A commit records submitted changes; it does **not** by itself prove who manually authored the code. C's **independent acceptance remains pending**. The points it enforces:
   - **Correspondence:** per case, the trusted `(input_mode, basename, fingerprint, as-of, kind)` is derived from the authoritative case definitions (`score_gov004.py::expected_case_identity`) and compared to the manifest; tier-provider settings must match the fixed configuration (`_tier_providers_match_fixed`); case/config/provenance/result and hash checks bind each report to its record.
   - **Counterfeit rejection:** conflicting mirror copies and bare authoritative metadata lines outside the header block are rejected (`_reject_counterfeit_metadata_outside_header`; canonical-record equality for durability mirrors).
   - **Unsuccessful-attempt accounting:** `replay_store.claim_start` records an exclusive, durable STARTED before dispatch under a cross-process lock; an unresolved start stays a non-completed denominator entry and blocks ID reuse; the scorer reports all started/completed attempts and separates retries.
 - **Baseline/team change.** Verification-tooling changes (R2/R3) in the supervised OpenCode repair session on C's evaluator (origin/hardening/repair by commit per above). The application product code is not the evaluator; the ledger and scorer are verification governance.
 - **Tradeoff.** Binding and duplicate-detection add complexity and refuse convenience shortcuts (e.g., reusing a run ID, or substituting a held-target artifact for an empty case); a stricter scorer can fail an otherwise "good-looking" package.
 - **Implementation status.** **Implemented** as verification tooling: original evaluator (C), hardening (`bb777d5`), R2/R3 repairs/regressions (`56bbe29`). **Deterministically enforced:** case/config/artifact binding, counterfeit rejection, exclusive durable starts, all-start accounting. **Residual:** the scorer cannot authenticate a human reviewer or decide general financial truth; the human score sheet is intentionally unfilled and **C's independent acceptance is pending**.
 - **Links.** Tests: `tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py`, `test_r2_r3_differential_pins.py`, `test_r3_replay_durability.py` (durable-before-dispatch, later-failure retention, unresolved start stays non-completed, exclusive same-ID claim); C harness `tests/member_c_verification/live/test_score_gov004_exitcodes.py` (PASS/FAIL/PENDING exit codes), `test_harness_selfcheck.py`. Source: `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py`, `replay_store.py`. Evidence: `docs/reviews/evidence/live-verification-2026-11-21/` (`gov004_starts.json`, `cohort.json`, `ai-review-proposed-scores.json`, `rescore-results.json`, `integrity.json`).
 - **Residual limitation.** The retained cohort used a narrow rubric that does **not** test general financial arithmetic; the AI-proposed 28/28 is a proposal, not C acceptance. Demonstration: the **retained live package** is re-scored from the repository; the scorer reports `PENDING` until a real reviewer supplies the score sheet, while a counterfeit/substituted artifact fails (`test_r2_02_held_target_substituted_for_empty_case_fails`, `test_r2_03_*`, `test_r3_04_unresolved_start_stays_noncompleted_and_blocks_reuse`).
 
 ### 8A.3a Concise intermediate context: a reversible cost/evidence tradeoff *(integrated at `adb4dfc`)*
 
 - **Concrete problem.** Verbose intermediate analyst reports are re-read by downstream agents, and debate prompts carried both the full history and a separate copy of the opponent's latest argument — the same evidence sent twice. The existing character/4 prompt guard bounded very large prompts but did not address this sub-threshold repetition.
 - **Design decision (feature `9102759`).** Advisory evidence-first brevity guidance (~450-word analysts, ~220-word Bull/Bear/risk): in `analysts/turn.py` appended to the **assembled system message**, in Bull/Bear/risk appended to their **assembled prompt strings**. Deterministic replacement of a duplicated opponent argument by a reference **only when the exact stripped text occurs in history** (**exact Python string-substring matching**); and a compaction safeguard that reconstructs the explicit copies and, if the reconstructed-original length exceeds `min(context_cap_tokens, compaction_threshold_tokens)*4`, passes the restored form to the existing guard. **No unconditional no-dangling guarantee:** a short argument can be replaced by a longer reference notice, so the reference form can exceed the guard target even when the restored original fits, and checking only the restored-original length can miss compaction of the reference form (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`). Reversible via `concise_intermediate_reports` (default True; env/programmatic False restores legacy).
 - **Deterministic vs advisory.** Flag/metadata plumbing, the exact-string reference, and the reconstruct-then-guard branch are deterministic; the word targets and evidence-preservation wording are **advisory** prompt guidance. **No new forced output/tool-payload truncation** is introduced (the existing guard may still trim narrative); it is not a guarantee that every evidence item survives compaction.
 - **Kept separate.** Not the existing per-prompt guard; not the proposed Slice C `CALL_CAP`/`BUDGET` controller (ADR-002 D3, unimplemented). Observed savings do not satisfy `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-002`.
 - **Tradeoff.** Shorter intermediate context can omit nuance the model would otherwise restate; the reference depends on exact text presence (no semantic dedup). Reversible configuration bounds the risk.
 - **Implementation status.** **Integrated at `adb4dfc` (PR #18 merge; ancestor of current HEAD `5672a79`).** The dangling-reference boundary (probe `docs/reviews/evidence/token-context-reference-probe-2026-11-24.json`), independent quality acceptance and prior approval remain **open**. Source changes touch files included in `prompt_hash`, so new-run `prompt_hash` differs; mode is recorded separately in `EffectiveConfig`.
 - **Measurements (E-reported; not rerun here).** Optimized 99,532 / 103,120 / 110,725 tokens (mean 104,459) vs historical mean 138,896.5 (24.7936%) and a same-day one-sample control 160,826 (35.0484%); single NVDA/2026-01-09 case, four analysts, English, 1+1 rounds, school `openai_compatible` + DeepSeek V4 Flash, empty memory, no portfolio, caching; exclusions and a failed attempt disclosed; **no ablation**, **no universal/runtime/quality claim**. Benchmark uses raw `graph.run_transient`, not `run_analysis_api`; `COMPLETED` is not product/check/semantic acceptance. Supervising review reproduced **49 offline tests** (not E's 1,797 full suite).
 - **Links.** Feature source (immutable): [`context.py`@9102759](https://github.com/kelepawuqiusi/CS5351/blob/9102759caaa59d778ba49cd57a1306f5f2ee5d88/tradingagents/agents/context.py), [`turn.py`@9102759](https://github.com/kelepawuqiusi/CS5351/blob/9102759caaa59d778ba49cd57a1306f5f2ee5d88/tradingagents/agents/analysts/turn.py), [test_token_input_reduction.py@9102759](https://github.com/kelepawuqiusi/CS5351/blob/9102759caaa59d778ba49cd57a1306f5f2ee5d88/tests/member_d_verification/test_token_input_reduction.py), [PR #18](https://github.com/kelepawuqiusi/CS5351/pull/18).  ### 8A.4 Demonstration types and originality claim
 
 Three distinct deliverables use this material; they are not interchangeable:
 
 - **Video — product demonstration.** Shows before/after behaviour (e.g., optional/empty portfolio, protected facts across stages, advisory-vs-authoritative status, a publication-failure or counterfeit negative) using recorded live **or clearly labelled scripted offline** material. It illustrates the mechanism; it does not itself prove originality or acceptance.
 - **Original-SE explanation.** Explains the project-specific design decisions above: why these facts must be protected across stages, why advisory text is separated from deterministic authority, and why evaluation evidence must bind case/config/artifact. The novelty claim rests on this adaptation and demonstrated effect, **not** on the use of standard techniques.
 - **Traceability/governance evidence.** The retained tests, evidence packages, and (when assembled by E) `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md` link requirement → component → test/evidence → monitor. Presence of files or green CI does not by itself prove a gate is enforced or a rubric passed.
 
 **Honesty boundary.** Standard techniques (immutability, hashing, atomic publication, ledgers, fail-closed checks) and compliance with course instructions alone do **not** establish originality. No experiment, approval, or ADD cycle is invented here; the demonstration thread reuses existing tests and retained artifacts. The honest limits (prompt grounding ≠ deterministic ownership enforcement; Q1–Q4 ≠ truth; scorer ≠ human acceptance) are stated above and must stay visible.

 # ADR 004 — Cumulative token admission beside the call cap (Alt-B settlement)
 
 - Status: **Proposed (architecture record 2026-11-24)**. A genuinely new design cycle for `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` (cumulative token budget). It **does not modify** the C2 evaluation (C1/C2/C3) in [ADR 001](001-portfolio-aware-cli.md), the call-cap design (ADR-002 D3, §15), or the concise-context record (ADR-003, still **Proposed**). Not implementation; D implementation and C acceptance pending.
 - Deciders: Member B (author), pending A (requirement meaning), C (verification), D (feasibility), E (evidence). Does not adopt requirements.
 - Scope: cumulative input+output token admission across all model-request paths, alongside §15's call cap. Detailed contracts: [interface-contracts.md](../interface-contracts.md) §15A; state: [memory-design.md](../memory-design.md) §10.
 
 > This is current design reasoning, not a measured experiment. No paid runs, no invented comparison.
 
 ## Context
 
 §15 bounds the **number** of model-request attempts (`CALL_CAP`) with monotonic, single-use call reservations. That is orthogonal to **token** consumption: a within-cap run can still spend unbounded tokens (long prompts, large outputs, retries, concurrency). `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001` requires a cumulative input+output budget with **reserve-before-dispatch**. `max_tokens=None` and the advisory 450/220-word targets are **not** finite output bounds. The provider-usage seam exists (`usage_metadata.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`) but `cli/stats_handler.py` zero-defaults missing fields, which must not be copied.
 
 ## Decision
 
 Adopt, as a **proposed** design, a per-run `AdmissionCoordinator` that checks the §15 call cap **and** a token ledger **atomically** (no partial grant), with these elements:
 
 1. **Defensible bounds, not estimates.** Admission requires a per-profile provider capability contract: a defensible **input upper bound** (exact tokenizer, or tokenizer-family + safety multiplier **justified for the complete supported request domain**; samples alone do not prove an upper bound), **tool/schema overhead** included, and a **finite enforced output allowance**. A profile lacking these is **UNSUPPORTED** (admission refuses; surfaced as a decision), never silently estimated. Character/4 is not admissible. The reservation is bound to the **final prepared request + config**, immutable after measurement.
 2. **Mutually exclusive ledger** K (known actual) / R (reserved/in-flight) / U (UNKNOWN retained). Admission: `K+R+U+(input_bound+output_allowance) <= TOKEN_BUDGET` **conditional on the bounds holding**; a violation is made visible, never hidden. `H=K+R+U` is **not** monotonic; cumulative counters are.
 3. **Alt-B settlement:** on **known** usage, move R→K with actual (unused allowance released; a decrease in H is intended); on **UNKNOWN**, move R→U (capacity retained, not reported as actual). **This version keeps U until finalization — no late U→K.**
 4. **Invariant/refusal/overage semantics:** a **bound/protocol violation** (actual > allowance) records actual (no clamp), halts admissions, propagates a typed `TokenBoundViolation` → `INTERNAL_ERROR` with a safe diagnostic; an **ordinary required-refusal** (cannot fit) → `BUDGET`. **No new serialized stop reason.** `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` precedence preserved; in-flight accounted before immutable finalization; single terminal; truthful durability.
-5. **Usage seam correctness:** admission happens **before** the provider request; usage is captured from the returned response **before** structured parsing can discard it (including parse-failure paths). `normalize_content` is post-response; `with_structured_output` builds a runnable and issues no request; notify-dispatch occurs at the real `.invoke`. Known settlement requires **valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ UNKNOWN.
+5. **Usage seam correctness:** admission happens **before** the provider request; usage is captured at the **chat-model `_create_chat_result` seam** (already overridden in `DeepSeekChatOpenAI`), which every routing — plain, `bind_tools`, `with_structured_output` — passes through **below** the structured parser, so raw provider usage is read **before** parsing can discard it (including parse-failure followed by fallback). `normalize_content` is post-response; `with_structured_output` builds a runnable and issues no request. The reservation binds the **final prepared request** (post-`_get_request_payload`, including provider-added fields) via an immutable `payload_fingerprint`. Known settlement requires **valid input and output usage**; missing/partial ⇒ UNKNOWN. Exactly-once via ticket state; SDK retries `max_retries=0`.
 6. **Call-cap coordination:** one atomic ticket; call grants are **never refunded** on invalidation (§15 monotonic), while **token** capacity **is** released on proven non-dispatch. Integration is a **targeted wrapper** of §15's entry point; §15 counting rules unchanged.
 
 ## Alternatives (genuinely distinct; current reasoning)
 
 - **Alt-A — conservative full-allowance retention.** A dispatched attempt **permanently charges its full allowance** even if known usage is smaller; measured usage is recorded **separately** as information. Simplest accounting; strictest (persistently under-admits after cheap calls); UNKNOWN is a non-issue since the allowance was never released.
 - **Alt-B — known-usage settlement with UNKNOWN retention (SELECTED).** On known settle, release unused allowance (R→K by actual); on UNKNOWN, retain capacity in U. Tighter capacity use; requires reliable usage capture + explicit UNKNOWN handling. **Selected** because it better matches `REQ-TA-NFR-COST-001`'s intent (count actual cumulative tokens, not permanently over-charge) while still reserving-before-dispatch and retaining UNKNOWN.
 - **Usage-only post-accounting (NON-COMPLIANT).** Admit *after* observing usage. Cannot reserve before dispatch and cannot bound concurrency; explicitly **not compliant** with COST-001. Not offered as a choice.
 
 **Tradeoff of the selection:** Alt-B's accuracy depends on the usage seam and bounds holding; a bound/protocol violation must be surfaced (it is). Alt-B is not "uniquely compliant" versus Alt-A — both reserve before dispatch and satisfy the reserve clause; Alt-A is more conservative and simpler, Alt-B uses capacity more efficiently. The choice reflects the requirement's "count actual tokens" intent, not a measured result.
 
 ## Consequences
 - **Positive:** a checkable cumulative bound with a precise ledger; violations visible; no new stop reason; §15 call semantics preserved; reversible/parked behind a config gate.
 - **Costs/limits:** requires the provider/profile bounds contract (UNSUPPORTED otherwise); bound violation may occur even under budget → `INTERNAL_ERROR`; empirical per-profile bound validity is separate evidence (E). Offline tests prove accounting logic, not deployed bounds. U retained to finalization (no late resolution) may overstate held capacity.
 - **Preserved:** C2 history; ADR-002 call semantics; ADR-003 Proposed status; no adoption of `TOKEN_BUDGET`/`CALL_CAP`/120000.
